title.zh: 卷十五 列傳第五 劉穆之 徐羨之 傅亮 檀道濟
title.en: Volume 15 Biographies 5: Liu Muzhi, Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji
title.raw: 卷十五 列傳第五 劉穆之 徐羨之 傅亮 檀道濟 Volume 15 Biographies 5: Liu Muzhi, Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji

sentences.zh: 劉穆之

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi

sentences.zh: 刘穆之，字道和，小字道人，东莞莒人也，世居京口。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi, styled Daohé, childhood name Daoren, was a man of Ju in Dongguan; his family had long lived at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, styled Daohé and known in youth as Daoren, came from Ju in Dongguan; his family had settled at Jingkou for generations.

sentences.zh: 初为琅邪府主簿，尝梦与宋武帝泛海遇大风，惊俯视船下，见二白龙挟船。

translations.literal: At first he served as chief clerk of the Langya commandery office; once he dreamed that he and Emperor Wu of Song were boating on the sea when a great wind arose; startled, he looked down from the boat and saw two white dragons flanking it.
translations.idiomatic: He began as chief clerk in the Langya commandery office. Once he dreamed that he and Emperor Wu of Song were sailing when a gale struck; alarmed, he looked over the side and saw two white dragons bracing the vessel.

sentences.zh: 既而至一山，山峰耸秀，意甚悦。

translations.literal: Presently they reached a mountain; its peaks rose lofty and fine, and he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they came to a mountain whose peaks stood tall and graceful, and he felt deep delight.

sentences.zh: 及武帝克京城，從何無忌求府主簿，無忌進穆之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the capital, Muzhi sought the post of chief clerk through He Wuji; Wuji recommended Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor captured the capital, Muzhi asked He Wuji to appoint him chief clerk, and Wuji put his name forward.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾亦識之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I know him too.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I know him as well.

sentences.zh: 」即馳召焉。

translations.literal: " He at once sent a fast messenger to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately dispatched a rider to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 時穆之聞京城有叫聲，晨出陌頭，屬與信會，直視不言者久之，反室壞布裳為褲往見帝，帝謂曰：「我始舉大義，須一軍吏甚急，誰堪其選？

translations.literal: At that time Muzhi heard shouting in the capital; at dawn he went out to the road, happened to meet the messenger, stared at him without speaking for a long while, returned home, tore his cloth robe into trousers, and went to see the Emperor. The Emperor said, "I have just raised the great cause and urgently need a military clerk — who is fit for the choice?
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi had heard clamor in the capital that morning. He went out to the road, met the messenger by chance, fixed his eyes on him and said nothing for a long while, then went home, ripped his cloth robe into trousers, and presented himself before the Emperor. The Emperor said, "I have just launched this great enterprise and urgently need a military clerk. Who can fill the role?

sentences.zh: 」穆之曰：「無見踰者。

translations.literal: " Muzhi said, "There is none who surpasses me.
translations.idiomatic: " Muzhi replied, "No one surpasses me.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿能自屈，吾事濟矣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor smiled and said, "If you can humble yourself, my affair will succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor smiled. "If you can stoop to this, my cause is won.

sentences.zh: 」即於坐受署。

translations.literal: " He thereupon received appointment on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: " Muzhi was appointed then and there.

sentences.zh: 從平建鄴，諸大處分，皆倉卒立定，並穆之所建，遂動見諮詢。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Jianye, every major disposition was settled in haste and established at once — all Muzhi's doing — and thereafter he was consulted at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: During the pacification of Jianye, every major decision was made on the fly and fixed at once, all at Muzhi's hand; from then on the Emperor consulted him constantly.

sentences.zh: 穆之亦竭節盡誠，無所遺隱。

translations.literal: Muzhi also exhausted his loyalty and held nothing back.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi gave his full loyalty and concealed nothing.

sentences.zh: 時晉綱寬弛，威禁不行，盛族豪家，負勢陵縱；

translations.literal: At that time Jin's net was slack and its prohibitions unenforced; great clans and powerful houses relied on their influence to ride over and flout the law;
translations.idiomatic: Jin's authority had grown lax and its laws went unenforced; great families and powerful houses used their influence to bully and defy order;

sentences.zh: 重以司馬元顯政令違舛，桓玄科條繁密。

translations.literal: added to this, Sima Yuanxian's orders were perverse and wrong, and Huan Xuan's statutes were dense and intricate.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yuanxian's government was erratic and corrupt, and Huan Xuan had piled statute upon statute.

sentences.zh: 穆之斟酌時宜，隨方矯正，不盈旬日，風俗頓改。

translations.literal: Muzhi weighed the times and corrected matters as needed; within less than ten days customs changed abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi adjusted policy to the moment and corrected abuses wherever they arose; in less than ten days the whole tone of public life shifted.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書祠部郎，復為府主簿、記室、錄事參軍，領堂邑太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat and again served as chief clerk, recorder, and recording secretary, while also holding the post of Administrator of Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat, resumed duties as chief clerk, recorder, and recording secretary, and concurrently governed Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 以平桓玄功，封西華縣五等子。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Baron of Xihua.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in suppressing Huan Xuan he received a fifth-rank barony at Xihua.

sentences.zh: 及揚州刺史王謐薨，帝次應入輔。

translations.literal: When Governor of Yangzhou Wang Mi died, by precedence the Emperor should have entered the capital to assist the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi, governor of Yangzhou, died, the Emperor was next in line to enter the capital as regent.

sentences.zh: 劉毅等不欲帝入，議以中領軍謝混為揚州，或欲令帝於丹徒領州，以內事付僕射孟昶。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and the others did not want the Emperor to enter; they debated making Central Army Commander Xie Hun governor of Yangzhou, or having the Emperor hold the province at Dantu while turning internal affairs over to Vice Director Meng Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi and his faction did not want the Emperor in the capital. Some proposed making Xie Hun, Central Army Commander, governor of Yangzhou; others wanted the Emperor to govern from Dantu while Meng Chang, Vice Director, handled court affairs.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書右丞皮沈以二議諮帝。

translations.literal: They sent Right Director of the Secretariat Pi Shen to consult the Emperor on the two proposals.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Pi Shen, Right Director of the Secretariat, to lay both plans before the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 沈先與穆之言，穆之偽如廁，即密疏白帝，言沈語不可從。

translations.literal: Shen first spoke with Muzhi; Muzhi feigned going to the privy, then secretly memorialized the Emperor that Shen's words must not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen spoke first with Muzhi, who pretended to need the privy and at once sent a secret note warning the Emperor not to accept Shen's advice.

sentences.zh: 帝既見沈，且令出外，呼穆之問焉。

translations.literal: After the Emperor had seen Shen and sent him out, he summoned Muzhi and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shen had been dismissed, the Emperor called Muzhi in and asked his view.

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「公今日豈得居謙，遂為守蕃將邪？

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "My lord, how can you now stand on humility and become a frontier general guarding a fief?
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said, "My lord, how can you afford modesty now and settle for life as a frontier commander?

sentences.zh: 劉、孟諸公俱起布衣，共立大義，事乃一時相推，非宿定臣主分也。

translations.literal: Lords Liu, Meng, and the rest all rose from common cloth; together they raised the great cause — their elevation was a moment's push, not an ancient fixed division of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, Meng, and the others all came up from common ranks and joined you in raising the cause; they were promoted in the heat of the moment, not by some old covenant of lord and subject.

sentences.zh: 力敵勢均，終相吞咀。

translations.literal: When strength is matched and power equal, in the end they devour one another.
translations.idiomatic: When power is evenly matched, one side eventually consumes the other.

sentences.zh: 揚州根本所系，不可假人。

translations.literal: Yangzhou is where the root lies — it cannot be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou is the root of the realm; you cannot hand it to anyone else.

sentences.zh: 前授王謐，事出權道，今若復他授，便應受制於人。

translations.literal: The earlier grant to Wang Mi came from expedient policy; if now another is appointed, you will fall under another's control.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi's appointment had been a temporary expedient; if you yield the post again, you will be ruled from outside.

sentences.zh: 一失權柄，無由可得。

translations.literal: Once authority is lost, there is no way to regain it.
translations.idiomatic: Lose the levers of power and you will never get them back.

sentences.zh: 公功高勳重，不可直置疑畏，便可入朝共盡同異。

translations.literal: Your merit is high and your honors heavy — you cannot simply invite suspicion and fear; you should enter court and share in settling all differences.
translations.idiomatic: Your achievements are too great to invite doubt without answer; go to court and settle every dispute face to face.

sentences.zh: 公至京邑，彼必不敢越公更授餘人。

translations.literal: When you reach the capital, they will not dare bypass you and appoint someone else.
translations.idiomatic: Once you are in the capital, none of them will dare pass you over for another appointment.

sentences.zh: 」帝從其言，由是入輔。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed his words and thereby entered to assist.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor took his advice and entered the capital as regent.

sentences.zh: 從廣固還拒盧循，常居幕中畫策。

translations.literal: Returning from Guanggu to resist Lu Xun, he often stayed in the tent to plan.
translations.idiomatic: On the return from Guanggu to oppose Lu Xun, he spent most of his time in headquarters drawing up plans.

sentences.zh: 劉毅等疾之，每從容言其權重，帝愈信仗之。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and the others resented him; they repeatedly spoke at leisure of his heavy authority, and the Emperor trusted and relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi and his circle resented him and kept remarking, in passing, on how much power he wielded; the Emperor only trusted him more.

sentences.zh: 穆之外所聞見，大小必白，雖閭里言謔，皆一二以聞。

translations.literal: Whatever Muzhi heard outside, great or small, he always reported; even village jokes he would relate one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Everything Muzhi heard outside, no matter how trivial, he reported — even village gossip reached the Emperor item by item.

sentences.zh: 帝每得人間委密消息以示聰明，皆由穆之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor received secret news from among the people to display his sharpness, it was through Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor seemed uncannily well informed about private affairs, Muzhi was the source.

sentences.zh: 又愛賓遊，坐客恒滿，布林目以為視聽，故朝野同異，穆之莫不必知。

translations.literal: He also loved entertaining guests; his seats were always full, and he spread eyes and ears among them as if for sight and hearing — thus whether court or countryside agreed or differed, Muzhi always knew.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to host guests and kept his hall full, planting listeners among them; court and countryside alike, he missed nothing.

sentences.zh: 雖親昵短長，皆陳奏無隱。

translations.literal: Even the faults of those close to him he reported without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: He reported even the failings of his intimates without hiding them.

sentences.zh: 人或譏之，穆之曰：「我蒙公恩，義無隱諱，此張遼所以告關羽欲叛也。」

translations.literal: Some mocked him for this; Muzhi said, "I owe the Duke a debt of grace and, by duty, cannot conceal — this is why Zhang Liao warned Guan Yu of intended rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Some ridiculed him. Muzhi said, "I owe the Duke my place and cannot keep secrets by duty — as Zhang Liao once warned Guan Yu of treachery."

sentences.zh: 帝舉止施為，穆之皆下節度，帝書素拙，穆之曰：「此雖小事，然宣佈四遠，願公小復留意。

translations.literal: In conduct and action the Emperor took Muzhi's direction; the Emperor's handwriting was naturally clumsy. Muzhi said, "Though this is a small matter, it is proclaimed to the four quarters — I hope my lord will give it a little attention.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor let Muzhi guide his conduct; his own handwriting was poor. Muzhi said, "It is a small thing, but edicts reach the four quarters — please give it some care.

sentences.zh: 」帝既不能留意，又稟分有在，穆之乃曰：「公但縱筆為大字，一字徑尺無嫌。

translations.literal: " The Emperor could not attend to it, and his allotted portion was what it was; Muzhi then said, "My lord need only write large characters freely — one character a foot across is no fault.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor could not be bothered, and his nature was fixed; Muzhi then said, "Write only large characters — a foot across each, if you like.

sentences.zh: 大既足有所包，其勢亦美。

translations.literal: Large enough to hold meaning, the form is also handsome.
translations.idiomatic: Size carries weight, and the look has dignity.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，一紙不過六七字便滿。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this; one sheet held no more than six or seven characters before it was full.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed; a single page rarely held more than six or seven characters.

sentences.zh: 穆之凡所薦達，不納不止。

translations.literal: Whatever Muzhi recommended, he did not stop until it was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi recommended someone, he pressed until the appointment was made.

sentences.zh: 常云：「我雖不及荀令君之舉善，然不舉不善。

translations.literal: He often said, "I am not the equal of Director Xun in promoting the good, but I never promote the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "I cannot match Director Xun in elevating talent, but I never elevate the unworthy."

sentences.zh: 」穆之與朱齡石並便尺牘，嘗于武帝坐與齡石並答書，自旦至日中，穆之得百函，齡石得八十函，而穆之應對無廢。

translations.literal: Muzhi and Zhu Lingshi were both quick with letters; once, seated with the Emperor, they answered correspondence together from dawn until midday — Muzhi finished a hundred bundles, Lingshi eighty, yet Muzhi's replies never lagged.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi and Zhu Lingshi both wrote at great speed. Once, seated with the Emperor, they answered mail from dawn to noon: Muzhi cleared a hundred stacks, Lingshi eighty, and Muzhi never fell behind.

sentences.zh: 遷中軍、太尉司馬，加丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Marshal of the Central Army and Grand Marshal, and additionally made Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Marshal of the Central Army under the Grand Marshal and was also appointed governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝西討劉毅，以諸葛長人監留府，疑其難獨任，留穆之輔之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched west against Liu Yi, he left Zhuge Changren to oversee the capital office, fearing he could not bear the burden alone, and kept Muzhi to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor marched west against Liu Yi, he left Zhuge Changren in charge of the capital but doubted he could manage alone, and kept Muzhi to help him.

sentences.zh: 加建威將軍，置佐吏，配給實力。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Establishes Might, with staff officers and a real allotment of troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Establishes Might, with a full staff and troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 長人果有異謀，而猶豫不能發，屏人謂穆之曰：「悠悠之言，雲太尉與我不平，何以至此？

translations.literal: Changren indeed harbored a different design, yet hesitated and could not act; sending others away, he said to Muzhi, "Loose talk says the Grand Marshal and I are at odds — how did it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Changren did plot treachery but could not bring himself to act. Dismissing attendants, he told Muzhi, "Rumor says the Grand Marshal and I are estranged — how did matters reach this point?

sentences.zh: 」穆之曰：「公泝流遠伐，以老母弱子委節下，若一豪不盡，豈容若此。

translations.literal: " Muzhi said, "My lord marched upstream on a distant campaign and left your aged mother and young children under his command — if a single man were disloyal, how could things stand thus?
translations.idiomatic: " Muzhi said, "You marched far upstream and left your mother and children in his care — if one man had wavered, things would not look like this.

sentences.zh: 」長人意乃小安，穆之亦厚為之備。

translations.literal: " Changren's mind was somewhat eased, and Muzhi also made thorough preparations.
translations.idiomatic: " Changren relaxed a little, while Muzhi quietly made every precaution.

sentences.zh: 長人謂所親曰：「貧賤常思富貴，富貴必踐危機。

translations.literal: Changren told those close to him, "In poverty one longs for wealth; in wealth one must tread crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Changren told his intimates, "The poor dream of riches; the rich walk on the edge of ruin.

sentences.zh: 今日思為丹徒布衣，不可得也。

translations.literal: Today I wish to be a common cloth wearer of Dantu — it cannot be had.
translations.idiomatic: Today I would gladly be a plain townsman of Dantu — and I cannot.

sentences.zh: 」帝還，長人伏誅。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor returned, Changren was executed.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor returned, Changren was put to death.

sentences.zh: 進前將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 帝西伐司馬休之，中軍將軍道憐知留任，而事無大小，一決穆之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched west against Sima Xiuzhi, Central Army Commander Dao Lian nominally held the capital, but matters great and small were all decided by Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Dao Lian commanded the capital in name, but Muzhi decided everything.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，領選，將軍、尹如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, put in charge of appointments; his generalship and governorship of Danyang remained.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with charge of appointments, retaining his general's rank and the Danyang governorship.

sentences.zh: 帝北伐，留世子為中軍將軍、監太尉留府。

translations.literal: On the northern expedition the Emperor left the heir as Central Army Commander overseeing the Grand Marshal's capital office.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaign the Emperor left the heir as Central Army Commander to oversee the capital headquarters.

sentences.zh: 轉穆之左僕射、領監軍中軍二府

translations.literal: Muzhi was transferred to Left Vice Director and put in charge of both the supervisory army and the central army offices
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi was made Left Vice Director and placed over both the supervisory army and central army offices

sentences.zh: 軍司，將軍、尹、領選如故，甲仗五十人入殿，入居東穆之內總朝政，外供軍旅，決斷如流，事無壅滯。

translations.literal: as army supervisor; his generalship, governorship, and charge of appointments were unchanged; fifty armed guards entered the hall with him. Within the eastern quarters he oversaw court government; outside he supplied the armies — decisions flowed like water and nothing piled up.
translations.idiomatic: as army supervisor, keeping his generalship, governorship, and appointment powers; fifty armed guards accompanied him into court. From the eastern offices he ran the government; outward he fed the armies — business moved without backlog.

sentences.zh: 賓客輻湊，求訴百端，內外諮稟，盈階滿室。

translations.literal: Guests gathered in crowds; petitions came from every direction; consultations inside and out filled the steps and packed the rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Clients thronged his doors; petitions arrived from every quarter; callers inside and out filled stair and hall.

sentences.zh: 目覽詞訟，手答箋書，耳行聽受，口並酬應，不相參涉，皆悉贍舉。

translations.literal: His eyes scanned lawsuits, his hand answered letters, his ears took reports, his mouth returned replies — none interfering with another, all fully discharged.
translations.idiomatic: He read lawsuits with his eyes, answered letters with his hand, listened with his ears, and spoke replies with his mouth — all at once, and all done.

sentences.zh: 又言談賞笑，彌日亙時，未嘗倦苦。

translations.literal: He also conversed, joked, and laughed from day into night without ever showing weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He talked and laughed from dawn to midnight and never showed fatigue.

sentences.zh: 裁有閒暇，手自寫書，尋覽篇章，校定墳籍。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a spare moment he copied books by hand, searched texts, and collated the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments he copied books, browsed texts, and collated the canon.

sentences.zh: 性奢豪，食必方丈，旦輒為十人饌，未嘗獨餐。

translations.literal: By nature he was lavish; his meals always filled a square table, and each morning he prepared food for ten — he never dined alone.
translations.idiomatic: He lived lavishly: every meal filled a square table, and each morning he ordered food for ten — he never ate alone.

sentences.zh: 每至食時，客止十人以還，帳下依常下食，以此為常。

translations.literal: Whenever he ate, if guests numbered fewer than ten, his staff still served the usual meal — this was his custom.
translations.idiomatic: If fewer than ten guests came, his household still laid the full spread — that was his rule.

sentences.zh: 嘗白帝曰：「穆之家本貧賤，贍生多闕，叨忝以來，雖每存約損，而朝夕所須，微為過豐，此外無一豪負公。」

translations.literal: Once he reported to the Emperor, "Muzhi's family was originally poor and low; provisions were often lacking. Since receiving undeserved favor, though I always try to economize, what I need morning and evening is slightly too ample; beyond that I owe the Duke not one whit."
translations.idiomatic: He once told the Emperor, "My family was poor; we often went without. Since your grace elevated me I have tried to be frugal, yet my daily needs are still rather rich — but beyond that I owe you nothing."

sentences.zh: 義熙十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yixi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Yixi (417).

sentences.zh: 帝在長安，本欲頓駕關中，經略趙、魏，聞問驚慟，哀惋者數日。

translations.literal: The Emperor was at Chang'an and had intended to halt in Guanzhong to plan against Zhao and Wei; when the news came he was shocked and grieved, mourning for several days.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was at Chang'an, intending to hold Guanzhong and strike toward Zhao and Wei; when word came he was stricken with grief for days.

sentences.zh: 以根本虛，乃馳還彭城。

translations.literal: Because the root was empty he hurried back to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital left bare he raced back to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以司馬徐羨之代管留台，而朝廷大事常決于穆之者，並悉北諮。

translations.literal: He put Marshal Xu Xianzhi in charge of the capital office, and major court affairs that had been decided by Muzhi were all referred north for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Xu Xianzhi over the capital, and every major decision that had rested with Muzhi was sent north for approval.

sentences.zh: 穆之前軍府文武二萬人，以三千配羨之建威府，餘悉配世子中軍府。

translations.literal: Muzhi's former army office had twenty thousand civil and military staff; three thousand were assigned to Xianzhi's Establishing Might office, the rest to the heir's Central Army office.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi's former staff of twenty thousand was split: three thousand to Xianzhi's Establishing Might command, the rest to the heir's central army.

sentences.zh: 追贈穆之開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Muzhi was posthumously granted an office equal to the Three Excellencies with full staff.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi was posthumously given an office equal to the Three Excellencies and a full staff.

sentences.zh: 帝又表天子曰：「臣聞崇賢旌善，王教所先，念功簡勞，義深追遠。

translations.literal: The Emperor also memorialized the Son of Heaven, "Your servant has heard that exalting the worthy and displaying goodness comes first in royal teaching, and remembering merit and selecting the toiling is the deeper meaning of honoring the distant past.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also memorialized the throne: "I have heard that exalting worthies and honoring goodness is the first duty of kings, and remembering service is the deepest form of reverence for the dead.

sentences.zh: 故司勳執策，在勤必記，德之休明，沒而彌著。

translations.literal: Therefore the Director of Merit records deeds — diligence is always noted; virtue in its brilliance shines more after death.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Merit inscribes every deed; merit shines brighter once the man is gone.

sentences.zh: 故尚書左僕射、前將軍臣穆之，爰自布衣，協佐義始，內竭謀猷，外勤庶政，密勿軍國，心力俱盡。

translations.literal: The former Left Vice Director and General of the Vanguard, your servant Muzhi, rose from common cloth, joined at the start of the righteous cause, exhausted counsel within and toiled in civil affairs without, serving the army and state in close trust with all his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director and former General of the Vanguard Muzhi rose from common cloth, joined me at the founding of our cause, gave counsel within and labor without, and gave heart and mind to army and state alike.

sentences.zh: 及登庸朝右，尹司京畿，敷贊百揆，翼新大猷。

translations.literal: When he ascended to the right of court and governed the capital region, he spread aid through the hundred offices and winged the great design.
translations.idiomatic: When he took high office and governed the capital, he steadied the hundred ministries and bore up the great design.

sentences.zh: 頃戎車遠役，居中作捍，撫寧之勳，實洽朝野，識量局致，棟幹之器也。

translations.literal: Recently, with the war-chariot on distant service, he held the center as bulwark; his merit in pacifying and settling truly reached court and countryside — a man of measure, scope, and pillar-strength.
translations.idiomatic: On the recent distant campaign he held the center as shield; his work in pacifying the realm reached every quarter — a man of judgment, scope, and pillar strength.

sentences.zh: 方宣贊盛化，緝隆聖世，忠績未究，遠邇悼心。

translations.literal: Just as he was to proclaim and assist the great transformation and bind up the sage age, his loyal achievement was not finished, and near and far mourn.
translations.idiomatic: He was just beginning to help spread the new order when his loyal service ended unfinished, and all mourn him.

sentences.zh: 皇恩褒述，班同三事，榮哀既備，寵靈已泰。

translations.literal: Imperial grace has praised and described him, ranking him with the Three Dignities; glory in life and mourning in death are complete, favor and spirit already abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The throne has already honored him with rank equal to the Three Dignities; glory in life and mourning in death are complete.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思尋，自義熙草創，艱患未弭，外虞既殷，內難亦薦，時屯世故，靡有寧歲。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects and searches: from the founding in Yixi, hardship was not yet stilled; outer alarm was pressing and inner trouble also repeated — the times were beset and the age knew no peace.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect: from our founding in Yixi troubles never ceased — threats abroad, crises within, year after year without rest.

sentences.zh: 臣以寡乏，負荷國重，實賴穆之匡翼之益。

translations.literal: Your servant, weak and lacking, bears the heavy burden of state and truly relied on Muzhi's bracing aid.
translations.idiomatic: I am weak and ill-equipped for the weight of empire, and I leaned on Muzhi's support.

sentences.zh: 豈唯讜言嘉謀，溢於人聽，若乃忠規密謨，潛慮帷幕，造膝詭辭，莫見其際。

translations.literal: It was not only that loyal words and fine plans overflowed what men heard; even loyal remonstrance and secret counsel, hidden thought within the curtain, words at the knee in subtle phrasing — none saw their edge.
translations.idiomatic: It was not only that his counsel overflowed public hearing; secret remonstrance within the curtain, subtle words at the knee — none saw how deep it ran.

sentences.zh: 事隔於皇朝，功隱於視聽者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Matters hidden from the imperial court and merit concealed from sight and hearing cannot be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: What he did unseen by court or public cannot be numbered.

sentences.zh: 所以陳力一紀，遂克有成，出征入輔，幸不辱命。

translations.literal: Therefore, exerting strength for a full cycle, he was able to succeed; on campaign and in assisting the throne, fortunately he did not disgrace the charge.
translations.idiomatic: For a full cycle he gave his strength and made success possible; on campaign and at court he never failed the trust placed in him.

sentences.zh: 微夫人之左右，未有寧濟其事者矣。

translations.literal: Without such a man at one's side, there would have been no settling of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Without a man like him at one's side, nothing would have been settled.

sentences.zh: 履謙居寡，守之彌固，每議及封爵，輒深自抑絕。

translations.literal: He kept humility and held to few desires, guarding them all the more firmly; whenever enfeoffment was discussed he deeply refused it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lived humbly and wanted little, guarding that stance all the more; whenever fiefs were discussed he refused them outright.

sentences.zh: 所以勳高當年，而茅土弗及，撫事永念，胡寧可昧。

translations.literal: Therefore though his merit stood highest in his day, he received no domain; touching the matter I forever recall — how could it be obscured?
translations.idiomatic: Thus though his merit was greatest in his time he received no fief; remembering this, how could I hide it?

sentences.zh: 謂宜加贈正司，追甄土宇。

translations.literal: It is fitting to add posthumous rank as regular director and grant domain in retrospect.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he receive posthumous rank as a regular director and a retrospective grant of domain.

sentences.zh: 俾忠貞之烈，不泯於身後，大賚所及，永旌于善人。

translations.literal: Let loyal steadfastness not perish after the body, and let great reward reach forever to mark the good.
translations.idiomatic: Let loyal steadfastness outlive the man, and let reward forever mark the good.

sentences.zh: 臣契闊屯夷，旋觀終始，金蘭之分，義深情感，是以獻其乃懷，布之朝聽。

translations.literal: Your servant, bound in long trial, now sees beginning and end; the bond of orchid and cassia, its righteousness deep in feeling — therefore I offer my inmost thoughts and spread them to the court's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Bound to him through long trial, I have seen his course from start to finish; our bond ran deep — therefore I lay my heart before the court.

sentences.zh: 」於是重贈侍中、司徒，封南昌縣侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was again posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Minister of Education and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Education and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，每歎憶之，曰：「穆之不死，當助我理天下。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the abdication he often sighed in memory of him, saying, "If Muzhi had not died, he would have helped me govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the throne the Emperor often sighed for him: "If Muzhi still lived, he would help me rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 可謂'人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁。

translations.literal: One may say, 'When a man of excellence perishes, the state is stricken.'
translations.idiomatic: Truly, 'When such a man dies, the state grows feeble.'"

sentences.zh: '」光祿大夫范泰對曰：「聖主在上，英彥滿朝，穆之雖功著艱難，未容便關興毀。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendor Fan Tai replied, "With a sage lord above and heroes filling court, though Muzhi's merit stood out in hardship, one cannot at once tie the state's rise and fall to him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendor Fan Tai replied, "A sage sits the throne and talent fills the hall; Muzhi's merit in hard times was great, but the realm's fate cannot hang on one man alone.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿不聞驥騄乎，貴日致千里耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor smiled and said, "Have you not heard of swift steeds? Their worth is that they run a thousand li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor smiled. "Have you never heard of a swift horse? Its worth is a thousand li in a day.

sentences.zh: 」帝后復曰：「穆之死，人輕易我。

translations.literal: " Later the Emperor again said, "Muzhi's death — men lightly presume upon me.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he said again, "Since Muzhi died, men take me lightly.

sentences.zh: 」其見思如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the degree to which he was missed.
translations.idiomatic: " That was how deeply he was missed.

sentences.zh: 以佐命元勳，追封南康郡公，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: As a founding merit minister he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Nankang with the posthumous title Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: As a founding minister he was posthumously made Duke of Nankang with the posthumous title Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 穆之少時，家貧誕節，嗜酒食，不修拘檢。

translations.literal: When Muzhi was young his family was poor and he held to unconstrained ways; he loved wine and food and did not keep to propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Muzhi's family was poor and he lived freely; he loved wine and food and cared little for decorum.

sentences.zh: 好往妻兄家乞食，多見辱，不以為恥。

translations.literal: He liked going to his wife's brothers' home to beg food and was often insulted, yet felt no shame.
translations.idiomatic: He often went to his wife's brothers to beg a meal and was frequently humiliated, yet felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 其妻江嗣女，甚明識，每禁不令往江氏。

translations.literal: His wife was a daughter of the Jiang clan and very clear-sighted; she always forbade him from going to the Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, a daughter of the Jiang clan, was sharp-minded and forbade him from visiting her brothers.

sentences.zh: 後有慶會，屬令勿來。

translations.literal: Later, when there was a celebration, she ordered him not to come.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when her family held a feast, she told him to stay away.

sentences.zh: 穆之猶往，食畢求檳榔。

translations.literal: Muzhi still went; after eating he asked for betel nut.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi came anyway, and after the meal asked for betel.

sentences.zh: 江氏兄弟戲之曰：「檳榔消食，君乃常饑，何忽須此？

translations.literal: The Jiang brothers teased him, saying, "Betel aids digestion — you are always hungry; why suddenly need this?
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang brothers mocked him: "Betel helps digestion — you're always starving; why want this now?

sentences.zh: 」妻復截發市肴饌，為其兄弟以餉穆之，自此不對穆之梳沐。

translations.literal: " His wife again cut off her hair to buy delicacies and had her brothers feed Muzhi; from then on she would not comb or wash before him.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife cut off her hair, sold it for food, and had her brothers serve Muzhi; afterward she refused to dress or groom in his presence.

sentences.zh: 及穆之為丹陽尹，將召妻兄弟，妻泣而稽顙以致謝。

translations.literal: When Muzhi became Governor of Danyang he was about to summon his wife's brothers; his wife wept and kowtowed to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi became governor of Danyang and meant to summon her brothers, his wife wept and kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「本不匿怨，無所致憂。

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "I never hid resentment — there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said, "I bear no hidden grudge — do not fear.

sentences.zh: 」及至醉飽，穆之乃令廚人以金柈貯檳榔一斛以進之。

translations.literal: " When they arrived drunk and sated, Muzhi ordered the kitchen to bring a gold tray holding a hu of betel.
translations.idiomatic: " When they came and feasted until drunk, he had the kitchen serve a gold tray with a full measure of betel.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年，車駕幸江甯，經穆之墓，詔致祭墓所。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia the imperial carriage visited Jiangning and passed Muzhi's tomb; an edict ordered sacrifice at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 25 the Emperor visited Jiangning, passed Muzhi's tomb, and ordered offerings at the grave.

sentences.zh: 長子慮之嗣，卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Lüzhi succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lüzhi inherited the title and died.

sentences.zh: 子邕嗣。

translations.literal: The son Yong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 先是郡縣為封國者，內史、相並于國主稱臣，去任便止。

translations.literal: Earlier, where commanderies and counties became fief-states, the internal administrator and chancellor both addressed the fief-lord as subject and ceased on leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when a commandery became a fief, its internal administrator and chancellor called themselves subjects to the lord and stopped on leaving office.

sentences.zh: 孝建中始革此制為下官致敬。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian era this system was first reformed so subordinate officials merely paid respect.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaojian era this was changed so subordinates only paid formal respect.

sentences.zh: 河東王歆之嘗為南康相，素輕邕。

translations.literal: Prince of Hedong Xinzhi had once been chancellor of Nankang and always looked down on Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hedong Xinzhi had once served as Nankang's chancellor and always despised Yong.

sentences.zh: 後歆之與邕俱豫元會並坐，邕嗜酒，謂歆之曰：「卿昔見臣，今能見勸一杯酒不？

translations.literal: Later Xinzhi and Yong both attended the New Year's assembly and sat together; Yong loved wine and said to Xinzhi, "You once saw me as subject — can you now offer me a cup?
translations.idiomatic: Later both attended the New Year court; Yong, drunk, said to Xinzhi, "You once treated me as your lord — will you now pour me a cup?

sentences.zh: 」歆之因斅孫皓歌答曰：「昔為汝作臣，今與汝比肩，既不勸汝酒，亦不願汝年。

translations.literal: " Xinzhi, mimicking Sun Hao's song, answered, "Once I was your subject; now I stand shoulder to shoulder with you — I will neither urge your wine nor wish you long years.
translations.idiomatic: " Xinzhi answered in Sun Hao's verse: "Once I served you; now we stand as equals — I will neither urge your wine nor wish you long life.

sentences.zh: 」邕性嗜食瘡痂，以為味似鰒魚。

translations.literal: " Yong by nature loved to eat scab crusts, finding the taste like abalone.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong had a taste for scab crusts, which he said tasted like abalone.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣孟靈休，靈休先患灸瘡，痂落在床，邕取食之。

translations.literal: Once he visited Meng Lingxiu; Lingxiu had earlier suffered moxibustion sores, and scabs had fallen on the bed — Yong picked them up and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Meng Lingxiu, he found scabs from moxibustion sores on the bed and ate them.

sentences.zh: 靈休大驚，痂未落者，悉褫取飴邕。

translations.literal: Lingxiu was greatly alarmed; scabs not yet fallen he stripped off and fed to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu was horrified and tore off scabs still on his skin to feed Yong.

sentences.zh: 邕去，靈休與何勖書曰：「劉邕向顧見噉，遂舉體流血。

translations.literal: When Yong left, Lingxiu wrote to He Qiu, "Liu Yong just now looked back and ate — my whole body bled.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong left, Lingxiu wrote He Qiu: "Liu Yong turned and devoured me until I bled all over.

sentences.zh: 」南康國吏二百許人，不問有罪無罪，遞與鞭，瘡痂常以給膳。

translations.literal: " About two hundred officials of the Nankang fief, guilty or not, were whipped in turn; scab crusts regularly supplied his meals.
translations.idiomatic: " Some two hundred Nankang officials, guilty or innocent, were whipped in rotation to supply his scab meals.

sentences.zh: 邕卒，子肜嗣，坐刀斫妻奪爵，以弟彪紹。

translations.literal: When Yong died his son Tong succeeded; for hacking his wife with a sword he lost the title, and the younger brother Biao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Tong succeeded, lost the title for attacking his wife with a sword, and the younger brother Biao inherited.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，降封南康縣侯、虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan in Qi he was reduced to Marquis of Nankang and made Tiger Guard Central Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Jianyuan's start he was reduced to Marquis of Nankang and made Tiger Guard Central Commander.

sentences.zh: 坐廟墓不修，削爵為羽林監。

translations.literal: For failing to maintain ancestral temples and tombs his nobility was stripped and he became Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For neglecting ancestral temples and tombs he lost his rank and became a forest guard.

sentences.zh: 又坐與亡弟母楊別居，楊死不殯葬，崇聖寺尼慧首剃頭為尼，以五百錢為買棺，以泥洹輿送葬，為有司奏，事寢不出。

translations.literal: Again, for living apart from the mother Yang of his dead younger brother, leaving Yang unburied when she died, and having the nun Huishou of Chongsheng Temple shave her head and buy a coffin for five hundred cash and send the body in a mud cart — reported by the authorities, the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: He was also reported for living apart from his dead brother's mother Yang, leaving her unburied, and having a nun buy a cheap coffin and cart her corpse away; the case was shelved.

sentences.zh: 中子 式之

translations.literal: Middle son Shizhi
translations.idiomatic: The middle son, Shizhi

sentences.zh: 穆之中子式之字延叔，為宣城、淮南二郡太守，犯贓貨，揚州刺史王弘遣從事檢校之。

translations.literal: Muzhi's middle son Shizhi, styled Yanshu, served as administrator of Xuancheng and Huainan; for embezzlement Governor of Yangzhou Wang Hong sent an investigator.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi's middle son Shizhi, styled Yanshu, governed Xuancheng and Huainan; when Wang Hong, governor of Yangzhou, sent men to investigate embezzlement

sentences.zh: 式之召從事謂曰：「還白使君，劉式之于國粗有微分，偷數百萬錢何有，況不偷邪。

translations.literal: Shizhi summoned the investigator and said, "Go tell the envoy: Liu Shizhi has some small standing in the state — what is stealing a few million cash, and what is not stealing?
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi summoned the investigator and said, "Tell the governor: Liu Shizhi has some small standing in the realm — what is a few million cash, and what is not stealing?

sentences.zh: 」從事還白弘，由此得停。

translations.literal: " The investigator returned and reported to Hong, and the inquiry was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The investigator reported back and the inquiry ended.

sentences.zh: 從征關洛有功，封德陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For merit on the Guan-Luo campaign he was enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Marquis of Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: For merit on the Guan-Luo campaign he received a fifth-rank marquisate at Deyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died with posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子 瑀

translations.literal: Son Yu
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu

sentences.zh: 子瑀字茂琳，始興王浚為南徐州，以瑀為別駕。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Maolin, when Prince of Shixing Jun held southern Xuzhou made Yu his chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Maolin, served as chief aide when Prince Jun of Shixing held southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑀性陵物護前，時浚征北府行參軍吳郡顧邁輕薄有才能，浚待之厚。

translations.literal: Yu by nature looked down on others and shielded his own faults; at the time Gu Mai of Wu, a staff officer of the Northern Headquarters, was frivolous but talented, and Jun treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was arrogant and protective of his own standing; Gu Mai of Wu, a northern staff officer, was clever but reckless, and Jun favored him.

sentences.zh: 瑀乃折節事邁，邁以瑀與之款盡，浚所言密事，悉以語瑀。

translations.literal: Yu then bent his manner to serve Mai; Mai, finding Yu intimate, told him everything Jun said in confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Yu humbled himself before Mai, who confided in him every secret Jun shared.

sentences.zh: 瑀與邁共進射堂下，忽顧左右索單衣幘，邁問其故，瑀曰：「公以家人待卿，言無不盡，卿外宣洩。

translations.literal: Yu and Mai together entered the archery hall below; suddenly Yu looked about and asked for a single robe and cap; Mai asked why. Yu said, "The lord treats you as family and hides nothing — yet you leak it abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the archery hall, Yu suddenly asked for a cap and robe. Mai asked why. Yu said, "The prince treats you as kin and tells you everything — yet you broadcast it outside.

sentences.zh: 我是公吏，何得不啟白之。

translations.literal: I am the lord's officer — how could I not report this?
translations.idiomatic: I am his officer — how could I not report you?

sentences.zh: 」浚大怒，啟文帝徙邁廣州。

translations.literal: " Jun was furious and memorialized Emperor Wen to exile Mai to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun was furious and had Emperor Wen exile Mai to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑀性使氣尚人，後為御史中丞，甚得志。

translations.literal: Yu by nature was overbearing and admired by others; later as Censor-in-Chief he was very satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was overbearing and loved deference; as Censor-in-Chief he had his wish.

sentences.zh: 彈蕭惠開云：「非才非望，非勳非德。

translations.literal: He impeached Xiao Huikai, saying, "Neither talent nor expectation, neither merit nor virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Xiao Huikai: "No talent, no standing, no merit, no virtue.

sentences.zh: 」彈王僧達云：「蔭藉高華，人品冗末。

translations.literal: " He impeached Wang Sengda, saying, "Pedigree lofty and splendid, character base and low.
translations.idiomatic: " He impeached Wang Sengda: "Pedigree high, character low.

sentences.zh: 」朝士莫不畏其筆端。

translations.literal: " Court gentlemen all feared his pen.
translations.idiomatic: " Courtiers feared his pen.

sentences.zh: 轉右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 年位本在何偃前，孝武初，偃為吏部尚書，瑀圖侍中不得。

translations.literal: His age and rank had originally stood before He Yan; at the start of Xiaowu's reign Yan became Minister of Personnel, and Yu schemed for Palace Attendant without success.
translations.idiomatic: He had outranked He Yan, but when Yan became Minister of Personnel under Emperor Xiaowu, Yu failed to win Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 與偃同從郊祀，時偃乘車在前，瑀策駟居後，相去數十步，瑀蹋馬及之，謂偃曰：「君轡何疾？

translations.literal: With Yan he attended suburban sacrifice; Yan rode in front, Yu drove four horses behind, several tens of paces apart; Yu spurred his horse to catch up and said to Yan, "Why is your rein so fast?
translations.idiomatic: At a suburban sacrifice Yan rode ahead and Yu drove four horses behind; Yu spurred up and asked, "Why such a fast rein?

sentences.zh: 」偃曰：「牛駿馭精，所以疾耳。

translations.literal: " Yan said, "The ox is swift and the driver skilled — therefore fast.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "A swift ox and a skilled driver — that is why.

sentences.zh: 」偃曰：「君馬何遲？

translations.literal: " Yan said, "Why is your horse slow?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked, "Why is your horse slow?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「騏驥羅於羈絆，所以居後」。

translations.literal: " He said, "The thoroughbred is bound by halter — therefore behind.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu answered, "A thoroughbred is hobbled — that is why I lag.

sentences.zh: 偃曰：「何不著鞭使致千里？

translations.literal: " Yan said, "Why not apply the whip to reach a thousand li?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "Why not lash it to run a thousand li?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「一蹙自造青雲，何至與駑馬爭路。

translations.literal: " He answered, "One kick already reaches blue clouds — why contend with a nag on the road?
translations.idiomatic: " Yu answered, "One kick lifts me to the clouds — why race a nag?

sentences.zh: 」然甚不得意，謂所親曰：「人仕宦，不出當入，不入當出，安能長居戶限上？

translations.literal: " Yet he was very discontent and told those close, "In office one should enter or leave — how can one long sit on the threshold?
translations.idiomatic: " Still he was bitter and told friends, "One should rise or fall in office — who can sit forever on the doorstep?

sentences.zh: 」因求益州。

translations.literal: " He therefore requested Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked for Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及行，甚不得意，至江陵，與顏竣書曰：「朱修之三世叛兵，一日居荊州，青油幕下，作謝宣明面目見向，使齋帥以長刀引吾下席，于吾何有，政恐匈奴輕漢耳。

translations.literal: On departure he was very discontent; reaching Jiangling he wrote to Yan Jun, "Zhu Xiuzhi was a rebel for three generations yet one day held Jingzhou; under the green-oil canopy he wore Xie Xuanyan's face toward me — had the steward drawn a long knife to pull me from my seat, what would it matter to me? I only fear the barbarians will despise Han.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving for office he was furious; at Jiangling he wrote Yan Jun: "Zhu Xiuzhi rebelled for three generations yet held Jingzhou in a day; under the green canopy he wore Xie Xuanyan's face toward me — if a steward had pulled me down with a long knife, what of it? I only fear the barbarians will despise Han.

sentences.zh: 」坐奪人妻為妾免官。

translations.literal: " For seizing another's wife as concubine he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " He was dismissed for taking another man's wife as concubine.

sentences.zh: 後為吳興太守，侍中何偃嘗案之云：「參伍時望。

translations.literal: Later as Administrator of Wuxing, Palace Attendant He Yan once reviewed him, saying, "Ranks among contemporary reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as administrator of Wuxing, He Yan reviewed him as "among middling reputations of the day."

sentences.zh: 」瑀大怒曰：「我于時望何參伍之有。

translations.literal: " Yu was furious and said, "What place have I among middling reputations?
translations.idiomatic: Yu raged: "What middling reputation am I?

sentences.zh: 」遂與偃絕。

translations.literal: " He broke with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " He broke with Yan.

sentences.zh: 族叔秀之為丹陽，瑀又與親故書曰：「吾家黑面阿秀遂居劉安眾處，朝廷不為多士。

translations.literal: Clansman Xiuzhi was Governor of Danyang; Yu again wrote friends, "Our family's dark-faced Axiu now sits where Liu An's crowd sat — the court is not rich in talent.
translations.idiomatic: When clansman Xiuzhi became governor of Danyang, Yu wrote friends: "Our dark-faced Axiu now sits where Liu An's crowd sat — the court lacks men.

sentences.zh: 」其年疽發背，何偃亦發背癕。

translations.literal: That year carbuncle broke out on his back; He Yan also developed a back abscess.
translations.idiomatic: That year a carbuncle broke out on his back; He Yan developed one too.

sentences.zh: 瑀疾已篤，聞偃亡，歡躍叫呼，於是亦卒。

translations.literal: Yu was already gravely ill; hearing Yan had died he leaped and shouted for joy, and then he too died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was dying; hearing Yan was dead he leaped and shouted with joy, then died himself.

sentences.zh: 諡曰剛。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Gang.

sentences.zh: 孫 祥

translations.literal: Grandson Xiang
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Xiang

sentences.zh: 祥字顯征，式之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiang, styled Xianzheng, was Shizhi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, styled Xianzheng, was Shizhi's grandson.

sentences.zh: 父敳，太宰從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Jiao served as Attendant in the Grand Preceptor's office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiao was an attendant in the Grand Preceptor's office.

sentences.zh: 祥少好文學，性韻剛疏，輕言肆行，不避高下。

translations.literal: Xiang in youth loved literature; his temperament was bold and rough, his speech reckless, not avoiding high or low.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang loved literature in youth; he was bold, blunt, and reckless toward all ranks.

sentences.zh: 齊建元中，為正員郎。

translations.literal: In Jianyuan of Qi he served as Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi Jianyuan he was a Regular Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 司徒褚彥回入朝，以腰扇鄣日，祥從側過，曰：「作如此舉止，羞面見人，扇障何益。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Chu Yanhui entered court shading the sun with a waist fan; Xiang passed beside him and said, "With such conduct, ashamed to face people — what good is fan-shading?
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Education Chu Yanhui entered court fanning himself, Xiang passed and said, "Behavior like that shames you before others — what good is the fan?

sentences.zh: 」彥回曰：「寒士不遜。

translations.literal: " Yanhui said, "A cold scholar lacks courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui said, "A poor scholar lacks manners.

sentences.zh: 」祥曰：「不能殺袁、劉，安得免寒士。」

translations.literal: " Xiang said, "Unable to kill Yuan and Liu, how can one escape being a cold scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang said, "If you could not kill Yuan and Liu, how are you not a cold scholar?"

sentences.zh: 永明初，撰宋書，譏斥禪代，尚書令王儉密以啟聞，上銜而不問。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongming he compiled the History of Song, mocking the abdication; Minister of Works Wang Jian secretly reported it; the Emperor harbored resentment but did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongming's start he wrote a History of Song that mocked the abdication; Wang Jian reported it secretly; the Emperor resented it but took no action.

sentences.zh: 為臨川王驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan, Marshal Who Quells the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan, Marshal Who Quells the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 祥兄整為廣州，卒官，祥就整妻求還資，事聞朝廷。

translations.literal: Xiang's elder brother Zheng was in Guangzhou and died in office; Xiang went to Zheng's wife to demand returned assets — the matter reached court.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Zheng died in office at Guangzhou, Xiang demanded his widow return the estate — the court heard of it.

sentences.zh: 又於朝士多所貶忽。

translations.literal: He also belittled many court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He also belittled many courtiers.

sentences.zh: 王奐為尚書僕射，祥與奐子融同載，行至中堂，見路人驅驢，祥曰：「驢，汝好為之，如汝人才，皆已令僕。

translations.literal: Wang Huan was Vice Director of the Secretariat; Xiang rode with Huan's son Rong; reaching the central hall they saw a man driving a donkey on the road. Xiang said, "Donkey, do your best — with talent like yours, all have become servants.
translations.idiomatic: Riding with Vice Director Wang Huan's son Rong, Xiang saw a man driving a donkey and said, "Donkey, work hard — men like you are all servants now.

sentences.zh: 」著連珠十五首，以寄其懷。

translations.literal: " He composed fifteen linked pearls to express his mind.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote fifteen linked-pearl poems to vent his feelings.

sentences.zh: 其譏議者云：「希世之寶，違時必賤，偉俗之器，無聖則淪。

translations.literal: Those he satirized said, "Treasures of the age, when the time is wrong must be cheap; instruments for a grand age, without a sage then sink.
translations.idiomatic: In satire he wrote: "Treasures of the age grow cheap when times turn; great instruments sink without a sage.

sentences.zh: 是以明玉黜于楚岫，章甫窮於越人。

translations.literal: Therefore bright jade is rejected from Chu's hills, and the zhangfu cap is useless to men of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Bright jade is cast out from Chu's hills; the court cap finds no buyer in Yue.

sentences.zh: 」有以祥連珠啟上，上令御史中丞任遐奏其過惡，付廷尉。

translations.literal: " Someone reported the linked pearls to the throne; the Emperor had Censor-in-Chief Ren Xia memorialize his faults and handed him to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone sent the poems to the throne; the Emperor had Censor-in-Chief Ren Xia charge him and handed him to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 上別遣敕祥曰：「我當原卿性命，令卿萬里思愆。

translations.literal: The Emperor separately sent an order to Xiang, "I will spare your life and send you ten thousand li to reflect on fault.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote separately: "I will spare your life and send you ten thousand li to repent.

sentences.zh: 卿若能改革，當令卿得還。

translations.literal: If you can reform, you may return.
translations.idiomatic: Reform yourself and you may come back.

sentences.zh: 」乃徙廣州。

translations.literal: " He was exiled to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 不得意，終日縱酒，少時卒。

translations.literal: Discontented, he drank all day and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter and drunk every day, he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 從父兄子 秀之

translations.literal: Son's father's elder brother's son Xiuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Xiuzhi

sentences.zh: 秀之字道寶，穆之從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi, styled Daobao, was Muzhi's father's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi, styled Daobao, was Muzhi's cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖爽，山陰令。

translations.literal: Grandfather Shuang was Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuang was magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 父仲道，余姚令。

translations.literal: Father Zhongdao was Magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongdao was magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 秀之少孤貧，十歲時與諸兒戲前渚，忽有大蛇來，勢甚猛，莫不顛沛驚呼，秀之獨不動，眾並異之。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was orphaned young and poor; at ten, playing with other boys by the foreshore, a great snake suddenly came with fierce force; all panicked and cried out, but Xiuzhi alone did not move — all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, at ten he played by the shore when a huge snake appeared; the other boys fled screaming, but Xiuzhi did not stir — all were astonished.

sentences.zh: 東海何承天雅相知器，以女妻之。

translations.literal: He Chengtian of Donghai knew and valued him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian of Donghai recognized his talent and gave him his daughter.

sentences.zh: 兄欽之為朱齡石右軍參軍，隨齡石敗沒，秀之哀戚不歡宴者十年。

translations.literal: Elder brother Qinzhi was Right Army staff officer to Zhu Lingshi; following Lingshi's defeat he perished — Xiuzhi mourned and did not feast for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Qinzhi followed Zhu Lingshi to defeat and death; Xiuzhi mourned ten years without feasting.

sentences.zh: 宋景平二年，除駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping he was made Commandant of Horse-Cap.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingping 2 he became Commandant of Horse-Cap.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，再為建康令，政績有聲。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia he twice served as Magistrate of Jiankang with noted achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanjia he twice governed Jiankang with a strong record.

sentences.zh: 孝武鎮襄陽，以為撫軍錄事參軍、襄陽令。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu held Xiangyang he made Xiuzhi Recording Secretary of the Pacification Army and Magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu held Xiangyang he made Xiuzhi recording secretary and magistrate there.

sentences.zh: 襄陽有六門堰，良田數千頃，堰久決壞，公私廢業。

translations.literal: Xiangyang had the Six-Gate Weir and several thousand qing of good fields; the weir had long burst and public and private business lay waste.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang's Six-Gate Weir irrigated thousands of qing of good land, but long broken, it had ruined public and private farming.

sentences.zh: 孝武遣秀之修復，雍部由是大豐。

translations.literal: Xiaowu sent Xiuzhi to repair it, and the Yong region thereafter greatly prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu sent Xiuzhi to repair it, and the Yong region flourished.

sentences.zh: 後除西戎校尉、梁南秦二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Later he was made Colonel of the Western Barbarians and Governor of Liang, Southern Qin, with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Colonel of the Western Barbarians and governor of Liang and Southern Qin with overall command.

sentences.zh: 漢川饑饉，秀之躬自儉約。

translations.literal: Han River suffered famine; Xiuzhi personally practiced frugality.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han River region starved, Xiuzhi lived frugally himself.

sentences.zh: 先是漢川悉以絹為貨，秀之限令用錢，百姓利之。

translations.literal: Earlier Han River used silk as currency; Xiuzhi restricted orders to use coin — the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: The region had traded in silk; he ordered coin instead, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大舉北侵，遣輔國將軍楊文德、巴西梓潼二郡太守劉弘宗受秀之節度，震盪汧隴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year a great northern invasion was launched; General Who Assists the State Yang Wende and Administrator of Brazil and Zitong Liu Hongzong were placed under Xiuzhi's command to shake Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 a great northern campaign was launched; Yang Wende and Liu Hongzong were placed under Xiuzhi to strike Qian and Long.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑逆，秀之即日起兵，求赴襄陽，司空南譙王義宣不許。

translations.literal: When the crown prince committed regicide Xiuzhi raised troops at once and asked to march to Xiangyang; Minister of Works Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince murdered the emperor, Xiuzhi raised troops and asked to march to Xiangyang; Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao refused.

sentences.zh: 事甯，遷益州刺史，折留奉祿二百八十萬付梁州鎮庫，此外蕭然。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was moved to Governor of Yizhou, leaving two million eight hundred thousand in salary in the Liang garrison treasury — otherwise he was bare.
translations.idiomatic: After order returned he became governor of Yizhou, depositing 2.8 million in salary in the Liang treasury and keeping nothing else.

sentences.zh: 梁、益豐富，前後刺史莫不大營聚畜，多者致萬金。

translations.literal: Liang and Yizhou were rich; former governors all amassed stores — some reached ten thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Yizhou were rich; past governors hoarded wealth, some amassing gold by the ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 所攜賓僚並都下貧子，出為郡縣，皆以苟得自資。

translations.literal: The staff he brought were all poor youths of the capital; sent out to commanderies and counties they all lived by grasping gain.
translations.idiomatic: His staff were poor youths from the capital who, sent to counties, lived by graft.

sentences.zh: 秀之為政整肅，遠近悅焉。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi governed with strict order; near and far were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi ruled with strict order and won approval near and far.

sentences.zh: 南譙王義宣據荊州為逆，遣徵兵於秀之，秀之斬其使。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan held Jingzhou in rebellion and sent to summon troops from Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi beheaded the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao rebelled in Jingzhou and summoned Xiuzhi's troops, Xiuzhi beheaded the messenger.

sentences.zh: 以起義功，封康樂縣侯，徙丹陽尹。

translations.literal: For rising in righteousness he was enfeoffed Marquis of Kangle and moved to Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: For joining the loyal cause he was made Marquis of Kangle and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 先是秀之從叔穆之為丹陽，與子弟聽事上宴，聽事柱有一穿，穆之謂子弟及秀之，汝等試以栗遙擲柱，入穿者後必得此郡。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiuzhi's clansman Muzhi as Governor of Danyang feasted with sons and nephews in the audience hall; a hole in an audience pillar — Muzhi told sons, nephews, and Xiuzhi, "Try throwing chestnuts at the pillar from afar; whoever enters the hole will later obtain this commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Muzhi, as Danyang governor, feasted kin in the hall where a pillar had a hole; he told them to throw chestnuts at it — whoever hit the hole would hold the post. Only Xiuzhi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 唯秀之獨入焉，其言遂驗。

translations.literal: Only Xiuzhi alone entered; the words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy came true.

sentences.zh: 時賒買百姓物不還錢，秀之以為非宜，陳之甚切。

translations.literal: At that time on credit purchase the people were not repaid; Xiuzhi thought it wrong and memorialized forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: People bought on credit and were not paid; Xiuzhi protested sharply.

sentences.zh: 雖納其言，竟不用。

translations.literal: Though his words were accepted, in the end they were not used.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view but never applied it.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時定制令，疑人殺長吏科，議者謂會赦宜以徙論。

translations.literal: At that time statutes were being set; on the statute for killing a superior officer, debaters said that on general amnesty exile should apply.
translations.idiomatic: While statutes were revised, debaters held that killing a superior should be commuted to exile on amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秀之以為「律文雖不顯人殺官長之旨，若遇赦但止徙論，便與悠悠殺人曾無一異。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi held that "though the law text does not plainly state the intent of killing an official superior, if on amnesty only exile is stopped, it differs not at all from ordinary murder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi argued: "Though the code does not spell out killing an official superior, to stop at exile on amnesty makes it no different from common murder.

sentences.zh: 人敬官長比之父母，行害之身雖遇赦，謂宜長付尚方，窮其天命，家口補兵」。

translations.literal: Men revere officials as they do parents; though the killer's person may meet amnesty, he should be handed to the Directorate for the term of natural life, and household members drafted as soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Men honor officials as parents; even if the killer is spared, he should die in the Directorate, and his household be drafted as soldiers."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 後為甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Later he was Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, Governor of Yong, with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Colonel Who Pacifies the Man and governor of Yong with overall command.

sentences.zh: 將徵為左僕射，會卒。

translations.literal: About to be summoned as Left Vice Director, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to be recalled as Left Vice Director when he died.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡忠成公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works with posthumous title Duke Zhongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Minister of Works with title Duke Zhongcheng.

sentences.zh: 秀之野率無風采，而心力堅正。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was plain and unadorned without grace, yet his will was firm and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was plain and graceless, but resolute and upright.

sentences.zh: 上以其蒞官清潔，家無餘財，賜錢二十萬，布三百疋。

translations.literal: The Emperor because he held office cleanly with no surplus wealth granted two hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, finding his office clean and his house empty, gave him 200,000 cash and 300 bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 傳封至孫，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed to the grandson; when Qi received the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief passed to his grandson; when Qi took the throne it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi

sentences.zh: 徐羨之字宗文，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi, styled Zongwen, was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi, styled Zongwen, came from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 祖甯，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Grandfather Ning was Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ning was Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 父祚之，上虞令。

translations.literal: Father Zuozhi was Magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuozhi was magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 羨之為桓修撫軍中兵參軍，與宋武帝同府，深相親結。

translations.literal: Xianzhi served as middle army staff officer to Huan Xiu's Pacification Army in the same office as Emperor Wu of Song and formed a deep bond.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi served on Huan Xiu's staff in the same office as Emperor Wu and became his close ally.

sentences.zh: 武帝北伐，稍遷太尉左司馬，掌留任，副貳劉穆之。

translations.literal: On the northern expedition he was gradually promoted to Left Marshal of the Grand Marshal, holding the capital in deputy to Liu Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign he rose to Left Marshal, holding the capital as Liu Muzhi's deputy.

sentences.zh: 帝議北伐，朝士多諫，唯羨之默然。

translations.literal: When the Emperor debated the northern expedition many court gentlemen remonstrated; only Xianzhi was silent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor debated the northern campaign, courtiers remonstrated; Xianzhi alone was silent.

sentences.zh: 或問何獨不言，羨之曰：「今二方已平，拓地萬里，唯有小羌未定。

translations.literal: Some asked why he alone did not speak; Xianzhi said, "The two regions are already pacified and territory extends ten thousand li — only the little Qiang are not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Xianzhi said, "Two regions are pacified and the realm stretches ten thousand li — only the Qiang frontier remains.

sentences.zh: 公寢食不安，何可輕豫其議。」

translations.literal: The Duke cannot eat or sleep in peace — how can one lightly join in the debate."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke cannot rest — how can I lightly join the debate?"

sentences.zh: 穆之卒，帝欲用王弘代之。

translations.literal: When Muzhi died the Emperor wished to use Wang Hong in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi died the Emperor wanted Wang Hong to replace him.

sentences.zh: 謝晦曰：「休元輕易，不若徐羨之。

translations.literal: Xie Hui said, "Xiuyuan is light and easy — he is not the equal of Xu Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui said, "Xiuyuan is too easygoing — Xu Xianzhi is better.

sentences.zh: 」乃以羨之為丹陽尹，總知留任，甲仗二十人出入，加尚書僕射。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi was therefore made Governor of Danyang with overall charge of the capital, twenty armed guards entering and leaving, and additionally Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi became governor of Danyang with full charge of the capital, twenty guards, and the vice directorship.

sentences.zh: 義熙十四年，軍人朱興妻周生子道扶，年三歲，先得癇病。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi a soldier's wife Zhou bore a son Daofu, age three, who first had epilepsy.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 14 soldier Zhu Xing's wife Zhou bore Daofu, age three, who had epilepsy.

sentences.zh: 周因其病，發掘地生埋之，為道扶姑雙女所告，周棄市。

translations.literal: Zhou because of the illness dug earth and buried him alive; Daofu's aunt the Shuang sisters reported it — Zhou was executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou buried him alive in the earth; his aunts reported her and she was executed.

sentences.zh: 羨之議曰：「自然之愛，豺狼猶仁，周之凶忍，宜加顯戮。

translations.literal: Xianzhi debated, "Natural love — even wolves and jackals have benevolence; Zhou's fierce cruelty deserves conspicuous execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi argued: "Even beasts love their young; Zhou's cruelty deserved public death.

sentences.zh: 臣以為法律之外，尚弘通理，母之即刑，由子明法。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that beyond the law one should still extend broad principle — the mother's execution comes from the son's clarifying the law.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond statute, principle still matters — the mother was punished because the son upheld law.

sentences.zh: 為子之道，焉有自容之地。

translations.literal: In the way of a son, where is room for self-comfort?
translations.idiomatic: As a son, where is room for comfort?

sentences.zh: 愚謂可特申之遐裔。

translations.literal: I deem it fitting to specially extend her to the far border.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that she be specially exiled to the far border.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝后失德，羨之等將謀廢立，而廬陵王義真多過，不任四海。

translations.literal: Later the Empress lost virtue; Xianzhi and the others planned deposition — Prince of Luling Yizhen had many faults and could not bear the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress lost virtue, Xianzhi and others plotted deposition; Prince Yizhen of Luling was unfit to rule.

sentences.zh: 乃先廢義真，然後廢帝。

translations.literal: They first deposed Yizhen, then deposed the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They deposed Yizhen first, then the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時謝晦為領軍，以府舍內屋敗應修理，悉移家人出宅，聚將士於府內。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Hui was Commandant of the Guard; because buildings in the office were ruined and needed repair, he moved all family out and gathered soldiers within.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, Commandant of the Guard, emptied his residence and packed the office with troops, citing repairs.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟以先朝舊將，威服殿省，且有兵眾，召入朝告之謀。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji, as an old general of the former dynasty feared in the palace with troops, was summoned to court and told the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji, an old general feared in the palace, was summoned and told the plan.

sentences.zh: 既廢帝，侍中程道惠勸立皇子義恭，羨之不許。

translations.literal: After deposing the Emperor, Palace Attendant Cheng Daohui urged establishing Prince Yigong; Xianzhi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: After the deposition, Cheng Daohui urged Prince Yigong; Xianzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 及文帝即位，改封南平郡公，固讓加封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended he was changed to Duke of Nanping and firmly declined further enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended, Xianzhi became Duke of Nanping and declined further honors.

sentences.zh: 有司奏車駕依舊臨華林園聽訟，詔如先二公權訊。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized that the imperial carriage should as before hear lawsuits at Hualin Garden; an edict followed the former practice of the two dukes' provisional hearings.
translations.idiomatic: Officials asked that the Emperor hear cases at Hualin as before; the edict followed the old provisional practice.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，羨之與傅亮歸政，三奏乃見許。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia Xianzhi and Fu Liang returned power — three memorials before permission.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 2 Xianzhi and Fu Liang returned power after three memorials.

sentences.zh: 羨之仍遜位，退還私第。

translations.literal: Xianzhi still yielded rank and withdrew to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi resigned and withdrew home.

sentences.zh: 兄子佩之及程道惠、吳興太守王韶之等，並謂非宜，敦勸甚苦。

translations.literal: Nephew Peizhi and Cheng Daohui, Administrator of Wuxing Wang Shaozhi, and others all said it was wrong and urged him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Peizhi, Cheng Daohui, Wang Shaozhi of Wuxing, and others urged him to return.

sentences.zh: 復奉詔攝任。

translations.literal: He again received edict to hold office provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted edict to resume office.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝以羨之、亮、晦旬月間再肆酖毒，下詔暴其罪，誅之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the Emperor, because Xianzhi, Liang, and Hui within a month twice used poison, issued an edict exposing their crimes and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 3, first month, the Emperor exposed their crimes for twice poisoning emperors within a month and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 爾日，詔召羨之至西明門外，時謝晦弟皭為黃門郎正直，報亮云：「殿中有異處分。

translations.literal: That day an edict summoned Xianzhi to outside the Western Bright Gate; at that time Hui's younger brother Jiao was Attendant at the Yellow Gate on duty and reported to Liang, "There is an unusual disposition in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day Xianzhi was summoned to the Western Bright Gate; Hui's brother Jiao, on duty at the Yellow Gate, warned Liang, "Something is wrong in the palace.

sentences.zh: 」亮馳報羨之，羨之乘內人問訊車出郭，步走至新林，入陶灶中自縊而死，年六十三。

translations.literal: " Liang raced to tell Xianzhi; Xianzhi rode the inner inquiry carriage out of the city, walked to Xinlin, entered a pottery kiln, and hanged himself — age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang warned Xianzhi, who rode an inner carriage out of the city, walked to Xinlin, hid in a kiln, and hanged himself at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 羨之初不應召，上遣領軍到彥之、右衛將軍王華追討。

translations.literal: At first Xianzhi did not answer the summons; the Emperor sent Commandant of the Guard Dao Yan and Right Guard General Wang Hua in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi ignored the summons, the Emperor sent Dao Yan and Wang Hua after him.

sentences.zh: 及死，野人以告，載屍付廷尉。

translations.literal: After death a commoner reported it; the corpse was delivered to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner found the body and it was sent to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 初，羨之年少時，嘗有一人來謂曰：「我是汝祖。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xianzhi was young, a man came and said, "I am your ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth a man came to Xianzhi and said, "I am your ancestor.

sentences.zh: 」羨之拜。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi bowed.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi bowed.

sentences.zh: 此人曰：「汝有貴相而有大厄，宜以錢二十八文埋宅四角，可以免災。

translations.literal: The man said, "You have a noble countenance but a great calamity — bury twenty-eight cash at the four corners of the house and you may escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "You have noble features but great disaster — bury twenty-eight coins at the house corners to escape it.

sentences.zh: 過此可位極人臣。

translations.literal: Pass this and you may reach the pinnacle of human rank.
translations.idiomatic: Survive that and you may reach the summit of rank.

sentences.zh: 」後羨之隨親之縣，住在縣內。

translations.literal: " Later Xianzhi followed a relative to a county and lived within the county office.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he stayed in a county office with a relative.

sentences.zh: 嘗暫出，而賊自後破縣，縣內人無免者，雞犬亦盡，唯羨之在外獲全。

translations.literal: Once he went out briefly; bandits broke the county from behind — none within escaped, even chickens and dogs were gone; only Xianzhi outside was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Once he stepped out briefly; bandits sacked the county and killed everyone inside — only Xianzhi outside survived.

sentences.zh: 又隨從兄履之為臨海樂安縣，嘗行經山中，見黑龍長丈餘，頭有角，前兩足皆具，無後足，曳尾而行。

translations.literal: Again following elder clansman Lüzhi to Lean of Linhai, traveling through the mountains he saw a black dragon more than a zhang long, horned, with both forelegs complete but no hind legs, dragging its tail as it went.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling with cousin Lüzhi through Linhai mountains he saw a black dragon over a zhang long, horned, with forelegs but no hind legs, dragging its tail.

sentences.zh: 及拜司空，守關將入，彗星辰見危南。

translations.literal: When he was appointed Minister of Works, guarding the pass about to enter, a comet appeared south of Weizi.
translations.idiomatic: When appointed Minister of Works and about to enter the pass, a comet appeared south of Weizi.

sentences.zh: 又當拜時，雙鸛集太極殿東鴟尾鳴喚，竟以凶終。

translations.literal: Again at the appointment two storks gathered on the eastern owl-tail of the Hall of Supreme Pole calling — in the end he met a violent end.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointment two storks cried on the Hall of Supreme Pole's eastern finial — he died violently in the end.

sentences.zh: 兄欽之子 佩之

translations.literal: Elder brother Qin's son Peizhi
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Peizhi

sentences.zh: 羨之兄欽之位秘書監。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's elder brother Qin reached Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's elder brother Qin became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 欽之子佩之輕薄好利，武帝以其姻戚，累加寵任，為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Qin's son Peizhi was frivolous and greedy for gain; the Emperor because of marriage ties repeatedly favored him and made him Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's son Peizhi was frivolous and greedy; as an in-law the Emperor favored him and made him governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 景平初，以羨之知權，頗豫政事，與王韶之、程道惠、中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛為黨。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingping, because Xianzhi held power Peizhi took part in government and formed a faction with Wang Shaozhi, Cheng Daohui, Secretariat Attendant Xing Antai, and Pan Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingping's start Peizhi joined politics through Xianzhi's power, allying with Wang Shaozhi, Cheng Daohui, Xing Antai, and Pan Sheng.

sentences.zh: 時謝晦久病連灸，不堪見客，佩之等疑其托疾有異圖，與韶之、道惠同載詣傅亮，稱羨之意，欲令作詔誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Hui was long ill with repeated moxibustion and could not receive guests; Peizhi and others suspected feigned illness and a different design, rode with Shaozhi and Daohui to Fu Liang, stating Xianzhi's intent to have an edict execute Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui was too ill to receive guests, Peizhi suspected a plot, visited Fu Liang with Shaozhi and Daohui, and urged an edict to kill Hui.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「己等三人同受顧命，豈可自相殘戮。

translations.literal: Liang said, "We three together received the dying charge — how can we slaughter one another?
