translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "We three received the dying charge together — we cannot kill one another.

sentences.zh: 」佩之等乃止。

translations.literal: " Peizhi and the others then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Peizhi and the others desisted.

sentences.zh: 羨之既誅，文帝特宥佩之，免官而已。

translations.literal: After Xianzhi was executed Emperor Wen specially pardoned Peizhi — removal from office only.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhi's death Emperor Wen spared Peizhi with dismissal only.

sentences.zh: 其冬佩之謀反事發被誅。

translations.literal: That winter Peizhi's rebellion was discovered and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Peizhi's rebellion was exposed and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 佩之弟 逵之

translations.literal: Peizhi's younger brother Kuizhi
translations.idiomatic: Peizhi's younger brother Kuizhi

sentences.zh: 佩之弟逵之尚武帝長女會稽宣公主，為彭城、沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: Kuizhi married the Emperor's eldest daughter Princess Xuan of Kuaiji and served as Administrator of Pengcheng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhi married Princess Xuan of Kuaiji and governed Pengcheng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 武帝諸子並幼，以逵之姻戚，將大任之，欲先令立功。

translations.literal: The Emperor's sons were all young; because Kuizhi was a marriage kin the Emperor meant to give him great trust and first let him win merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's sons were young; as an in-law he meant to trust Kuizhi after merit.

sentences.zh: 及討司馬休之，使統軍為前鋒，待克當即授荊州，於陣見害。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he commanded the army as vanguard; when victory came he was to receive Jingzhou — he was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the vanguard against Sima Xiuzhi he was to receive Jingzhou on victory — he was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 追贈中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子湛之。

translations.literal: Son Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 逵之子 湛之

translations.literal: Kuizhi's son Zhanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhi's son Zhanzhi

sentences.zh: 湛之字孝源，幼孤，為武帝所愛。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi, styled Xiaoyuan, was orphaned young and beloved by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi, styled Xiaoyuan, was orphaned young and raised in the Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 常與江夏王義恭寢食不離帝側。

translations.literal: He often slept and ate with Prince of Jiangxia Yigong without leaving the Emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: He often slept and ate with Prince Yigong of Jiangxia at the Emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，詔以公主一門嫡長，且湛之致節之胤，封枝江縣侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu an edict because the princess's house was chief in direct descent and Zhanzhi was heir of Kuizhi's integrity enfeoffed him Marquis of Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 3, as chief line of the princess's house and heir to Kuizhi's integrity, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: 數歲與弟淳之共車行，牛奔車壞，左右人馳來赴之。

translations.literal: A few years later riding with younger brother Chunzhi the ox bolted and the cart broke; attendants rushed up.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, riding with brother Chunzhi, the ox bolted and the cart broke; attendants rushed up.

sentences.zh: 湛之先令取弟，眾咸歎其幼而有識。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi first ordered them to take his brother; all sighed at his youth and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi ordered them to save his brother first; all marveled at his judgment in youth.

sentences.zh: 及長頗涉文義，善自位待，事祖母及母以孝聞。

translations.literal: When grown he dipped into letters and meaning, knew how to maintain position, and was known for filial service to grandmother and mother.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he read widely, kept his place well, and was famed for filial care of grandmother and mother.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，以為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia he was made Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanjia he became Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 祖母年老，辭以朝直不拜。

translations.literal: Grandmother was aged; he declined on grounds of court duty and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His aged grandmother made him decline court duty.

sentences.zh: 後拜秘書監。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會稽公主身居長嫡，為文帝所禮，家事大小必諮而後行。

translations.literal: Princess of Kuaiji as eldest in direct descent was honored by Emperor Wen; household matters great and small were always consulted before action.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Kuaiji, eldest in direct descent, was honored by Emperor Wen; no household matter moved without her counsel.

sentences.zh: 西征謝晦，使公主留止台內，總攝六宮，每有不得意，輒號哭，上甚憚之。

translations.literal: On the western expedition against Xie Hui the princess was kept inside the capital to oversee the six palaces; whenever displeased she wailed — the Emperor greatly feared her.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Xie Hui the princess stayed in the capital over the six palaces; when displeased she wailed — the Emperor feared her.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝微時，貧陋過甚，嘗自往新洲伐荻，有納布衣襖等，皆是敬皇后手自作。

translations.literal: Earlier when the Emperor was lowly he was extremely poor; once he went to Xinzhou to cut reeds himself — padded cloth coats and the like were all hand-made by Empress Dowager Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In poverty the Emperor once cut reeds at Xinzhou; padded coats were sewn by Empress Zhang herself.

sentences.zh: 武帝既貴，以此衣付公主曰：「後世若有驕奢不節者，可以此衣示之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was exalted he gave these clothes to the princess, saying, "If later there is one proud and lavish beyond measure, show him these clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When elevated he gave the clothes to the princess: "If any descendant grows proud and wasteful, show them these coats.

sentences.zh: 」湛之為大將軍彭城王義康所愛，與劉湛等頗相附。

translations.literal: " Zhanzhi was loved by Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and attached himself to Liu Zhan and others.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhanzhi was favored by Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and joined Liu Zhan's circle.

sentences.zh: 及得罪，事連湛之。

translations.literal: When guilt fell, the affair touched Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang fell, Zhanzhi was implicated.

sentences.zh: 文帝大怒，將致大辟。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was greatly angry and was about to impose capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was furious and meant to execute him.

sentences.zh: 湛之憂懼無計，以告公主。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was anxious without plan and told the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi, desperate, told the princess.

sentences.zh: 公主即日入宮，及見文帝，因號哭下床，不復施臣妾之禮。

translations.literal: The princess entered the palace that day; seeing Emperor Wen she wailed and fell from the bed, no longer using subject-wife rites.
translations.idiomatic: The princess entered court that day, wailed, and fell from the bed, abandoning subject-wife decorum.

sentences.zh: 以錦囊盛武帝納衣，擲地以示上曰：「汝家本賤貧，此是我母為汝父作此納衣。

translations.literal: She took a brocade pouch holding the Emperor's padded coat, threw it to the ground to show the Emperor and said, "Your house was originally base and poor — this is the padded coat my mother made for your father.
translations.idiomatic: She produced the Emperor's old padded coat in a brocade pouch and threw it down: "Your house was poor — this is the coat my mother sewed for your father.

sentences.zh: 今日有一頓飽食，便欲殘害我兒子。

translations.literal: Today after one full meal you would destroy my son.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after one good meal, you would destroy my son.

sentences.zh: 」上亦號哭，湛之由此得全。

translations.literal: " The Emperor also wailed; Zhanzhi thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor wept too; Zhanzhi was spared.

sentences.zh: 再遷太子詹事，尋加侍中。

translations.literal: He was again moved to Tutor of the Heir and soon added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became Tutor of the Heir and soon Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 湛之善尺牘，音辭流暢；

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was skilled at letters; his words flowed smoothly;
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi wrote elegantly and spoke with ease;

sentences.zh: 貴戚豪強，產業甚厚，室宇園池，貴游莫及，伎樂之妙，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: as noble kin and powerful house his estates were very thick, halls and gardens none among the gentry matched, music and performers foremost of the age.
translations.idiomatic: as a great noble his estates were vast, his halls and gardens unmatched, his performers the finest of the age.

sentences.zh: 門生千餘，皆三吳富人子，姿質端美，衣服鮮麗。

translations.literal: More than a thousand retainers, all rich sons of the Three Wu, handsome in bearing, bright in dress.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand retainers — rich sons of the Three Wu, handsome and finely dressed.

sentences.zh: 每出入行游，塗巷盈滿。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out the streets were packed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad the streets filled.

sentences.zh: 泥雨日，悉以後車載之。

translations.literal: On muddy rainy days he loaded them all in rear carts.
translations.idiomatic: On muddy days he carried them all in trailing carts.

sentences.zh: 文帝每嫌其侈縱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen often disliked his extravagance and license.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen often resented his extravagance.

sentences.zh: 時安成公何勖，無忌之子，臨汝公孟靈休，昶之子也，並名奢豪，與湛之以肴膳器服車馬相尚，都下為之語曰：「安成食，臨汝飾。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Ancheng He Qiu, Wuji's son, and Duke of Linru Meng Lingxiu, Chang's son, were both famed for luxury and rivaled Zhanzhi in food, vessels, dress, horses, and carriages — the capital said, "Ancheng eats, Linru adorns.
translations.idiomatic: Duke He Qiu of Ancheng and Duke Meng Lingxiu of Linru were famed for luxury and rivaled Zhanzhi in food, dress, and equipage — the capital said, "Ancheng feeds, Linru dresses.

sentences.zh: 」湛之美兼何、孟。

translations.literal: " Zhanzhi's beauty combined He and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhanzhi outdid both He and Meng.

sentences.zh: 勖官至侍中，追諡荒公。

translations.literal: Qiu reached Palace Attendant; posthumous title Duke Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu reached Palace Attendant; posthumous title Duke Huang.

sentences.zh: 靈休善彈棋，官至秘書監。

translations.literal: Lingxiu was skilled at pitch-pot and reached Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu excelled at pitch-pot and became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湛之後遷丹陽尹，加散騎常侍，以公主憂不拜。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was later moved to Governor of Danyang with additional Cavalier Attendant; because of the princess's mourning he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi later became governor of Danyang and Cavalier Attendant but declined during the princess's mourning.

sentences.zh: 過葬，復授前職。

translations.literal: After mourning he resumed the former posts.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed office.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，范曄等謀反，湛之始與之同，後發其事，所陳多不盡，為曄等款辭所連。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Fan Ye and others plotted rebellion; Zhanzhi at first joined them, later exposed the affair — what he stated was incomplete and he was tied by their confessions.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 Fan Ye plotted rebellion; Zhanzhi joined then exposed it, but his confession was incomplete and Ye's testimony implicated him.

sentences.zh: 有司以湛之關豫逆黨，事起積歲，末乃歸聞，多有蔽匿，請免官削爵，付廷尉。

translations.literal: The authorities because Zhanzhi was connected to the rebel faction, the affair lasting years and only at the end reported, with much concealment, requested removal from office, stripping of nobility, and delivery to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials asked to strip his rank and send him to court for years of concealed involvement in treason.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 湛之詣闕上疏請罪，以為「初通其謀，為誘引之辭，曄等並見怨咎，規相禍陷。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi went to court and memorialized guilt, holding that "at first joining their plot was enticement in words; Ye and the others all bore resentment and schemed mutual ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi memorialized guilt: "At first I was drawn by words; Ye and the others resented me and sought to ruin me together.

sentences.zh: 又昔義康南出之始，敕臣入相伴慰，殷懃異意，頗形言旨。

translations.literal: Again when Yikang first went south the edict ordered me to enter and comfort him — warm intent appeared plainly in words.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang first went south I was ordered to comfort him — his warmth was plain in speech.

sentences.zh: 遺臣利刃，期以際會。

translations.literal: He left me a sharp blade, expecting a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: He left me a sharp blade, expecting a meeting.

sentences.zh: 臣苦相諫譬，深加拒塞，以為怨憤所至，不足為虞，便以關啟，懼成虛妄。

translations.literal: I bitterly remonstrated and deeply refused, thinking resentment had gone too far and was not to be feared; I reported it lest it prove false.
translations.idiomatic: I refused and remonstrated, thinking his rage harmless; I reported it lest it prove empty.

sentences.zh: 非為納受，曲相蔽匿。

translations.literal: It was not receiving and concealing by bending.
translations.idiomatic: I did not accept or hide anything.

sentences.zh: 又令申情范曄，釋中間之憾，致懷蕭思話，恨婚意未申。

translations.literal: Again ordered to convey feeling to Fan Ye, release middle grievances, and convey regret to Xiao Sihua that marriage intent was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I was also told to reconcile with Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua over broken marriage plans.

sentences.zh: 謂此僥倖，亦不宣達。

translations.literal: I deemed such luck not to be proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: I thought such luck unworthy of mention.

sentences.zh: 陛下敦惜天倫，彰于四海，蕃禁優簡，親理咸通。

translations.literal: Your Majesty cherishes heaven's kin, shown in the four seas; fief prohibitions are generous and kin affairs all reach through.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cherishes kin throughout the realm; fiefs are generous and family ties remain open.

sentences.zh: 又昔蒙眷顧，不容自絕，音翰信命，時相往來。

translations.literal: Again formerly under gracious regard I could not cut myself off — letters and commands came and went in season.
translations.idiomatic: Under your grace I could not cut myself off — letters and orders passed between us.

sentences.zh: 或言少意多，旨深文淺，辭色之間，往往難測。

translations.literal: Some words held little intent and much meaning, purpose deep and text shallow — between word and color often hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Some words held much meaning in little text — tone and intent were hard to read.

sentences.zh: 臣顧惟心無邪悖，故不稍以自嫌，慺慺丹實，具如此啟。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that my heart has no rebellion — therefore I did not shrink from self-suspicion; loyal red truth is fully as in this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I know my heart holds no treason — I did not hide from suspicion; my loyalty is as stated.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑下，情匪木石，豈不知醜點難嬰，伏劍為易，而靦然視息，忍此餘生，實非苟吝微命，假延漏刻。

translations.literal: Your servant though dull and low, feeling is not wood or stone — how does one not know shame is hard to bear and falling on the sword is easy, yet calmly draw breath and endure this remaining life — truly not from stinginess with a slight life borrowed for a leaking moment.
translations.idiomatic: I am no stone — I know shame and that the sword is easy; yet I breathe on, not from clinging to a leaking life.

sentences.zh: 誠以負戾灰滅，貽恥方來，貪及視息，少自披訴。

translations.literal: Truly because ruin and offense would extinguish to ash, shame would reach the future — greedy still for breath, I briefly lay open my plea.
translations.idiomatic: Ruin would ash my name and shame my heirs — yet I beg breath to plead.

sentences.zh: 乞蒙隳放，伏待鈇鑕。

translations.literal: I beg destruction and release, to await axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: I beg punishment and await the axe.

sentences.zh: 」上優詔不許。

translations.literal: " A gracious edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: " A gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，服闋，轉中書令、太子詹事，出為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, mourning ended, he was moved to Director of the Secretariat and Tutor of the Heir, and sent out as Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24, mourning ended, he became Director of the Secretariat and Tutor of the Heir, then governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 善政俱肅，威惠並行。

translations.literal: Good government was all strict; authority and kindness went together.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was strict and fair; authority and kindness went together.

sentences.zh: 廣陵舊有高樓，湛之更修整之，南望鍾山。

translations.literal: Guangling formerly had a high tower; Zhanzhi further repaired it, facing south toward Bell Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling had an old tower; Zhanzhi rebuilt it facing Bell Mountain.

sentences.zh: 城北有陂澤，水物豐盛，湛之更起風亭、月觀，吹台、琴室，果竹繁茂，花藥成行。

translations.literal: North of the city were marshes rich in aquatic life; Zhanzhi further raised Wind Pavilion, Moon View, Flute Terrace, and Zither Hall — fruit and bamboo lush, flowers and herbs in rows.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city lay rich marshes; he added Wind Pavilion, Moon View, Flute Terrace, and Zither Hall amid fruit, bamboo, and flowers.

sentences.zh: 招集文士，盡遊玩之適。

translations.literal: He gathered literary gentlemen and fully enjoyed wandering pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered literati and took every pleasure of the place.

sentences.zh: 時有沙門釋惠休善屬文，湛之與之甚厚。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Hui Xiu was skilled at composition; Zhanzhi was very close to him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Hui Xiu wrote well; Zhanzhi was close to him.

sentences.zh: 孝武命使還俗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu ordered him returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered him to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 本姓湯，位至揚州從事史。

translations.literal: Original surname Tang; he reached Staff Officer of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Born Tang, he became staff officer of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，湛之入為丹陽尹、領太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Zhanzhi entered as Governor of Danyang and Tutor of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 Zhanzhi returned as governor of Danyang and Tutor of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，魏太武帝至瓜步，湛之與皇太子分守石頭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Wei Emperor Taiwu reached Guabu; Zhanzhi with the crown prince divided defense of Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 Wei Emperor Taiwu reached Guabu; Zhanzhi and the crown prince defended Shitou.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，魯爽兄弟率部曲來奔，爽等軌子也，湛之以為廟算特所獎納，不敢苟申私怨，乞屏田里。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Lu Shuang and brothers led their followers to defect — Shuang and the others were Gui's sons; Zhanzhi because the temple calculation specially rewarded and accepted them dared not press private grievance and begged retirement to fields.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 Lu Shuang and brothers defected — sons of Gui; Zhanzhi, rewarded by court calculation, dared not press private grudges and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Refused.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書僕射，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Commandant Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director and Commandant Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令何尚之以湛之國戚，任遇隆重，欲以朝政推之。

translations.literal: At that time Director He Shangzhi because Zhanzhi was imperial kin and heavily favored wished to push court government to him.
translations.idiomatic: Director He Shangzhi, as Zhanzhi was kin and favored, wanted to yield court affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 湛之以令事無不總，又以事歸尚之。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi because the Director's affairs were all summed and again returned affairs to Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi, finding the Director controlled everything, returned affairs to Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 互相推委，御史中丞袁淑奏並免官。

translations.literal: Mutually pushing responsibility, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Shu memorialized to dismiss both from office.
translations.idiomatic: They shoved responsibility back and forth until Censor Yuan Shu asked both be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 詔乃使湛之與尚之並受辭訴。

translations.literal: An edict then had Zhanzhi and Shangzhi both receive lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had both receive lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 尚之雖為令，而以朝事悉歸湛之。

translations.literal: Though Shangzhi was Director, court affairs all returned to Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shangzhi was Director, court affairs all went to Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 初，劉湛伏誅，殷景仁卒，文帝任沈演之、庾仲文、范曄等，後又有江湛、何瑀之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Liu Zhan was executed and Yin Jingren died, Emperor Wen trusted Shen Yanzhi, Yu Zhongwen, Fan Ye, and later Jiang Zhan and He Ruozhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zhan's death and Yin Jingren's demise, Emperor Wen trusted Shen Yanzhi, Yu Zhongwen, Fan Ye, then Jiang Zhan and He Ruozhi.

sentences.zh: 自曄誅，仲文免，演之、瑀之並卒，至是江湛為吏部尚書，與湛之並居權要，世謂之江、徐。

translations.literal: After Ye was executed Zhongwen was removed, Yanzhi and Ruozhi both died — by then Jiang Zhan was Director of Personnel and with Zhanzhi both held power — the age called them Jiang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye died, Yanzhi and Ruozhi followed; Jiang Zhan became Director of Personnel and with Zhanzhi shared power — the age spoke of Jiang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 上每疾，湛之輒侍醫藥。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor was ill Zhanzhi always attended with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor fell ill Zhanzhi attended with medicine.

sentences.zh: 二凶巫蠱事發，上欲廢劭，賜浚死，而孝武無寵，故累出外藩，不得停都下。

translations.literal: When the two villains' witchcraft affair broke out the Emperor wished to depose Shao and grant Jun death, but Xiaowu had no favor and was repeatedly sent to outer fiefs, unable to stay in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When witchcraft by the two villains broke out the Emperor meant to depose Shao and kill Jun, but unfavored Xiaowu was kept in outer fiefs.

sentences.zh: 南平王鑠、建平王宏並被愛，而鑠妃即湛妹，湛勸上立之，征鑠自壽陽入朝。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanping Shuo and Prince of Jianping Hong were both loved; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's sister — Zhanzhi urged establishing him and summoned Shuo from Shouyang to court.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Shuo of Nanping and Hong of Jianping were favored; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's sister — Zhanzhi urged making Shuo heir and summoned him from Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 至又失旨，欲立宏，嫌其非次，議久不決。

translations.literal: When he arrived he again missed the Emperor's intent; the Emperor wished to establish Hong but disliked the order of succession — debate long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo again displeased the Emperor; the Emperor turned to Hong but hesitated over succession — debate dragged on.

sentences.zh: 與湛之議，或連日累夕。

translations.literal: Debating with Zhanzhi, sometimes for days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: He debated with Zhanzhi for days and nights.

sentences.zh: 每夜，使湛之自執燭繞壁檢行，慮有竊聽者。

translations.literal: Each night he had Zhanzhi himself hold a candle and walk the wall checking, fearing eavesdroppers.
translations.idiomatic: Each night he made Zhanzhi walk the walls with a candle, fearing listeners.

sentences.zh: 劭入弑之旦，其夕上與湛之屏人語，至曉猶未滅燭。

translations.literal: The morning Shao entered to regicide, that evening the Emperor spoke with Zhanzhi behind closed doors until dawn without extinguishing candles.
translations.idiomatic: The night Shao murdered the Emperor, he talked with Zhanzhi behind closed doors until dawn, candles unextinguished.

sentences.zh: 湛之驚起趣北戶，未及開，見害，時年四十四。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi startled and rose toward the north door; before it opened he was killed — age forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi fled toward the north gate; before it opened he was killed at forty-four.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，追贈司空，諡曰忠烈公。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu ascended he was posthumously granted Minister of Works with posthumous title Duke Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously made him Minister of Works with title Duke Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 子聿之為元凶所殺。

translations.literal: Son Yuzhi was killed by the crown prince regicide.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuzhi was killed by the regicide crown prince.

sentences.zh: 聿之子孝嗣。

translations.literal: Yuzhi's son Xiaosi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi's son Xiaosi.

sentences.zh: 湛之孫 孝嗣

translations.literal: Zhanzhi's grandson Xiaosi
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi's grandson Xiaosi

sentences.zh: 孝嗣字始昌。

translations.literal: Xiaosi, styled Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi, styled Shichang.

sentences.zh: 父被害，孝嗣在孕，母年少，欲更行，不願有子，自床投地者無算，又以擣衣杵舂其腰，並服墮胎藥，胎更堅。

translations.literal: When his father was killed Xiaosi was in the womb; mother was young and wished to remarry and not bear a child — she threw herself from the bed countless times and pounded her waist with a clothes-beater, also taking abortifacients — the fetus held all the firmer.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was killed Xiaosi was unborn; his young mother wished to remarry and tried every abortive means — the child held firm.

sentences.zh: 及生，故小字遺奴。

translations.literal: At birth therefore his childhood name was Leftover Slave.
translations.idiomatic: Hence his childhood name Leftover Slave.

sentences.zh: 幼而挺立。

translations.literal: From infancy he stood upright.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he stood straight.

sentences.zh: 八歲襲爵枝江縣公，見宋孝武，升階流涕，迄于就席。

translations.literal: At eight he inherited the Marquisate of Zhijiang; seeing Emperor Xiaowu of Song he wept ascending the steps until taking seat.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he inherited Zhijiang; meeting Emperor Xiaowu he wept from the steps to his seat.

sentences.zh: 帝甚愛之，尚康樂公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly loved him; he married Princess of Kangle and was made Commandant of Horse-Cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor loved him; he married Princess of Kangle and became Commandant of Horse-Cap.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，以登殿不著韎，為書侍御史蔡准所奏，罰金二兩。

translations.literal: In Taishi he ascended the hall without gaiters and was impeached by Secretary Attendant Cai Zhun — fined two liang of gold.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi he entered court without gaiters; Cai Zhun fined him two liang of gold.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣姑適東莞劉舍，舍兄藏為尚書左丞，孝嗣往詣之。

translations.literal: Xiaosi's aunt married Liu She of Dongguan; She's elder brother Zang was Left Director of the Secretariat — Xiaosi went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: His aunt married Liu She of Dongguan; She's brother Zang, Left Director, received Xiaosi's visit.

sentences.zh: 藏退謂舍曰：「徐郎是令僕人，三十餘可知，汝宜善自結。

translations.literal: Zang withdrew and told She, "Attendant Xu is material for Director and Vice Director — in thirty years you will know; you should bind yourself to him well.
translations.idiomatic: Zang told She privately, "Xu is future Director material — in thirty years you'll see; bind yourself to him.

sentences.zh: 」升明中，為齊高帝驃騎從事中郎，帶南彭城太守，轉太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: " In Shengming he served as staff officer to Qi Emperor Gao, Marshal Who Quells the Barbarians, concurrently Administrator of Southern Pengcheng, then Counselor in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Shengming he served Qi Emperor Gao's staff, then as counselor in the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，累遷長兼侍中。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan in Qi he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Jianyuan's start he rose to Acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 善趨步，閑容止，與太宰褚彥回相埒。

translations.literal: Skilled in quick step and easy bearing, he matched Grand Preceptor Chu Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful in gait and bearing, he matched Grand Preceptor Chu Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉謂人曰：「徐孝嗣將來必為宰相。

translations.literal: Director Wang Jian told others, "Xu Xiaosi will in future certainly become Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Jian said, "Xu Xiaosi will become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 」轉御史中丞。

translations.literal: " Moved to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 武帝問儉曰：「誰可繼卿？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu asked Jian, "Who can succeed you?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu asked Jian, "Who succeeds you?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「臣東都之日，其在徐孝嗣乎。」

translations.literal: " Jian said, "On the day I leave the eastern capital, is it not Xu Xiaosi?"
translations.idiomatic: " Jian answered, "When I leave the eastern capital — Xu Xiaosi."

sentences.zh: 出為吳興太守，儉贈孝嗣四言詩曰：「方軌叔茂，追清彥輔，柔亦不茹，剛亦不吐。

translations.literal: Sent out as Administrator of Wuxing, Jian gave Xiaosi a four-character poem: "Square-track Shumao, pursuing clarity Yanfu — soft yet does not chew, hard yet does not spit.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving for Wuxing, Jian gave him a poem praising firm yet flexible character.

sentences.zh: 」時人以比蔡子尼之行狀也。

translations.literal: " Men of the time compared it to Cai Zini's conduct record.
translations.idiomatic: " Men compared it to Cai Zini's character sketch.

sentences.zh: 在郡有能名。

translations.literal: In the commandery he had a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In office he earned a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 王儉亡，上征孝嗣為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian died the Emperor summoned Xiaosi as Minister of Five Arms.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian died Xiaosi was summoned as Minister of Five Arms.

sentences.zh: 其年，敕撰江左以來儀典，令諮受孝嗣。

translations.literal: That year an edict compiled rites and ceremonies since the eastward crossing and ordered consultation with Xiaosi.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict compiled rites since the eastward crossing and consulted Xiaosi.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Tutor of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he became Tutor of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 從武帝幸方山。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu to Fang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu to Fang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕經始此山之南，復為離宮，應有邁靈丘。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I began this south of the mountain and again made a detached palace — there should surpass Lingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I began building south of this mountain and added a detached palace — it should surpass Lingqiu.

sentences.zh: 」靈丘山湖，新林苑也。

translations.literal: Lingqiu was Mountain Lake, New Forest Park.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqiu meant Mountain Lake, New Forest Park.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣答曰：「繞黃山，款牛首，乃盛漢之事。

translations.literal: Xiaosi answered, "Encircling Yellow Mountain and lingering at Oxhead — that was Han grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi answered, "Encircling Yellow Mountain and lingering at Oxhead — that was Han grandeur.

sentences.zh: 今江南未廣，願陛下少更留神。

translations.literal: Today the south of the river is not yet broad — I hope Your Majesty will for a little longer keep mind.
translations.idiomatic: The south is not yet broad — I hope Your Majesty will wait.

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor stopped.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良甚善之。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiling Ziliang was very fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jiling favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 曆吏部尚書，右軍將軍，領太子左衛率，台閣事多以委之。

translations.literal: He served as Director of Personnel, General of the Right Army, and Commander of the Heir's Left Guard — palace affairs were mostly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of Personnel, General of the Right Army, and Commander of the Heir's Left Guard — most palace affairs rested with him.

sentences.zh: 初在率府，晝臥齋北壁下，夢兩童子遽云：「移公床。

translations.literal: At first in the guard office he slept by day on the north wall of his study; he dreamed two boys hurriedly saying, "Move the lord's bed.
translations.idiomatic: Once sleeping by the north wall of his study he dreamed two boys saying, "Move the lord's bed.

sentences.zh: 」孝嗣驚起，聞壁有聲，行數步而壁崩壓床。

translations.literal: " Xiaosi startled and rose; hearing sound in the wall he walked several paces and the wall collapsed on the bed.
translations.idiomatic: " He woke; the wall collapsed on the bed moments later.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，即本號開府儀同三司，讓不受。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu he was granted on his existing title an office equal to the Three Excellencies with full staff and declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 4 he was offered an office equal to the Three Excellencies and declined.

sentences.zh: 時連年魏軍動，國用虛乏，孝嗣表立屯田。

translations.literal: At that time Wei armies moved year after year and state use was empty; Xiaosi memorialized to establish garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei campaigning yearly and the treasury empty, Xiaosi memorialized for garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 帝已寢疾，兵事未已，竟不行。

translations.literal: The Emperor was already bedridden and military affairs not yet ended — in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was already bedridden and war continued — it was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 及崩，受遺托，重申開府之命，加中書監。

translations.literal: At death he received the dying trust and again affirmed the order for an office equal to the Three Excellencies, adding Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the Emperor's death he received the regency and again accepted rank equal to the Three Excellencies plus Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永元初輔政，自尚書下省出住宮城南宅，不得還家。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongyuan assisting government he left the Secretariat's lower offices and lodged at the southern residence of the palace, unable to return home.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan's start he left the Secretariat and lodged at the palace's south residence, unable to go home.

sentences.zh: 帝失德，孝嗣不敢諫；

translations.literal: The Emperor lost virtue; Xiaosi did not dare remonstrate;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor lost virtue; Xiaosi dared not remonstrate;

sentences.zh: 及江祏誅，內懷憂恐，然未嘗表色。

translations.literal: when Jiang Shi was executed he harbored worry and fear within, yet never showed it in expression.
translations.idiomatic: when Jiang Shi was executed he was inwardly afraid but never showed it.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光反，眾懷惶惑，見孝嗣入宮乃安，然群小用事，不能制也。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang rebelled the crowd was fearful and unsettled; seeing Xiaosi enter the palace they were reassured — yet petty men held power and he could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an rebelled the court panicked; Xiaosi's entry calmed them — yet petty men held power and he could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 時孝嗣以帝終亂天常，與沈文季俱在南掖門，欲要文季以門為應，四五目之，文季輒亂以他語，孝嗣乃止。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaosi because the Emperor would finally overturn heaven's constant order, with Shen Wenji together at the Southern Flanking Gate, wished to win Wenji to respond with the gate — four or five times he signaled with his eyes; Wenji always diverted with other words — Xiaosi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking the Emperor would overturn order, Xiaosi at the Southern Flanking Gate tried to win Shen Wenji to open the gate — Wenji evaded him and Xiaosi gave up.

sentences.zh: 進位司空，固讓。

translations.literal: Advanced to Minister of Works and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Minister of Works, he declined.

sentences.zh: 求解丹陽尹，不許。

translations.literal: Requested release from Governor of Danyang — not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave the Danyang governorship — refused.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣文人，不顯同異，名位雖大，故得未及禍。

translations.literal: Xiaosi was a literary man who did not display sides; though rank was great he therefore did not reach disaster in time.
translations.idiomatic: A literary man who showed no faction, his great rank delayed his ruin.

sentences.zh: 虎賁中郎將許准有膽力，陳說事機，勸行廢立。

translations.literal: Tiger Guard Central Commander Xu Zhun had courage and force; he stated the situation and urged deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Guard Commander Xu Zhun, bold and forceful, urged deposition.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣遲疑，謂必無用干戈理，須少主出遊，閉城門，召百僚集議廢之。

translations.literal: Xiaosi hesitated, saying surely there was no reason to use arms — one must wait for the young lord to go out on tour, close the city gates, summon the hundred offices to assemble and debate deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi hesitated, saying arms were needless — wait for the young emperor's outing, close the gates, and assemble officials to depose him.

sentences.zh: 雖有此懷，終不能決。

translations.literal: Though he had this intent, in the end he could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: He had the thought but could never decide.

sentences.zh: 群小亦稍憎孝嗣，勸帝除之。

translations.literal: Petty men also gradually resented Xiaosi and urged the Emperor to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men grew to hate Xiaosi and urged the Emperor to kill him.

sentences.zh: 其冬，孝嗣入華林省，遣茹法珍賜藥，孝嗣容色不異，謂沈昭略曰：「始安事，吾欲以門應之，賢叔若同，無今日之恨。

translations.literal: That winter Xiaosi entered Hualin Office; Ru Fazhen was sent to grant poison. Xiaosi's expression did not change; he told Shen Zhaolue, "On the Shi'an affair I wished to respond with the gate — if worthy uncle had agreed, there would be no today's regret.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Ru Fazhen brought poison in Hualin Office. Unchanged, Xiaosi told Shen Zhaolue, "On Yaoguang's rebellion I meant to open the gate — had you agreed, I would not die today.

sentences.zh: 」少能飲酒，飲藥至鬥余方卒，乃下詔言誅之。

translations.literal: " Able to drink a little, he drank the drug to over a dou before dying — then an edict said he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Able to drink, he swallowed a dou of poison before dying — then an edict declared him executed.

sentences.zh: 于時凡被殺者，皆取其蟬冕，剝其衣服。

translations.literal: At that time all who were killed had their cicada crowns taken and clothes stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Those killed had their crowns taken and clothes stripped.

sentences.zh: 眾情素敬孝嗣，得無所侵。

translations.literal: Public feeling had long honored Xiaosi — his body was not violated.
translations.idiomatic: The people revered Xiaosi — his body was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 長子演，尚齊武帝女武康公主，位太子中庶子，第三子況，尚明帝女山陰公主，並拜駙馬都尉，俱見殺。

translations.literal: Eldest son Yan married Qi Emperor Wu's daughter Princess Wukang, post Commander of the Heir's Household; third son Kuang married Emperor Ming's daughter Princess Shanyin — both Commandants of Horse-Cap — all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Yan and third son Kuang, both imperial sons-in-law, were killed with him.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣之誅，眾人懼，無敢至者，唯會稽魏溫仁奔赴，以私財營喪事，當時稱之。

translations.literal: At Xiaosi's execution all feared and none dared come — only Wei Wenren of Kuaiji rushed to attend and paid for the funeral from private wealth — men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death none dared attend — only Wei Wenren of Kuaiji paid for the funeral from his own purse, and was praised.

sentences.zh: 初，孝嗣復故封，使故吏吳興丘叡筮之，當傳幾世。

translations.literal: At first when Xiaosi restored the old fief he had former clerk Qiu Rui of Wuxing divine how many generations it would pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaosi restored his fief he had former clerk Qiu Rui of Wuxing divine how many generations would inherit.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「怨不終尊身。

translations.literal: Rui said, "Resentment — not to the end honor the body.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "Resentment — honor will not last the body out."

sentences.zh: 」孝嗣容色甚惡，徐曰：「緣有此慮，故令卿決之。」

translations.literal: " Xiaosi's expression was very bad; slowly he said, "Because I had this worry, I had you decide it."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi's face darkened. "That is why I asked you."

sentences.zh: 中興元年，和帝贈孝嗣太尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing Emperor He posthumously granted Xiaosi Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongxing 1 Emperor He posthumously made Xiaosi Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 二年，改葬宣德太后，詔增班劍四十人，加羽葆、鼓吹，諡曰文忠，改封餘幹縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year, changing burial of Empress Dowager Xuande, an edict added forty halberds of the guard, plumes and canopy, drums and pipes — posthumous title Wenzhong, changed fief to Duke of Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, reburying Empress Dowager Xuande, an edict added guard halberds, canopy, and music — posthumous title Wenzhong, fief changed to Duke of Yugan.

sentences.zh: 子緄，仕梁，位侍中，太常，信武將軍，諡頃子。

translations.literal: Son Gun served Liang as Palace Attendant, Minister of Ceremonies, General Who Trusts in Military Affairs — posthumous title Duke Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Son Gun served Liang as Palace Attendant and Minister of Ceremonies — posthumous title Duke Qing.

sentences.zh: 緄子君蒨字懷簡，幼聰朗好學，尤長丁部書，問無不對。

translations.literal: Gun's son Junqian, styled Huaijian, was clever and fond of learning from youth, especially skilled in the Ding section of texts — asked, none went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Gun's son Junqian, styled Huaijian, was clever, learned, and master of classical texts — no question stumped him.

sentences.zh: 善弦歌，為梁湘東王鎮西諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Skilled at string songs; he served as Counselor on the staff of Prince of Xiangdong, Marshal Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at song, he served Prince of Xiangdong, Marshal Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 頗好聲色，侍妾數十，皆佩金翠，曳羅綺，服玩悉以金銀。

translations.literal: He rather loved sound and color; several tens of concubines all wore gold and kingfisher, trailing silk gauze — dress and play all in gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: He loved pleasure; dozens of concubines wore gold, jade, and silk — all finery was gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 飲酒數升便醉，而閉門盡日酣歌。

translations.literal: Drinking several sheng he was drunk and closed the door drinking and singing all day.
translations.idiomatic: A few sheng of wine made him drunk; he shut his doors and sang all day.

sentences.zh: 每遇歡謔，則飲至鬥。

translations.literal: Whenever mirth ran high he drank to a dou.
translations.idiomatic: In high spirits he drank a full dou.

sentences.zh: 有時載伎肆意遊行，荊楚山川，靡不畢踐。

translations.literal: Sometimes he loaded performers and wandered at will — Jing-Chu mountains and rivers, none he did not traverse.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he roamed Jing-Chu with performers and missed no scenic place.

sentences.zh: 朋從游好，莫得見之。

translations.literal: Friends and companions could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Friends could rarely find him.

sentences.zh: 時襄陽魚弘亦以豪侈稱，於是府中謠曰：「北路魚，南路徐。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Hong of Xiangyang was also famed for luxury — the office sang, "Fish on the north road, Xu on the south road.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hong of Xiangyang was also famed for luxury — the office sang, "Fish north, Xu south.

sentences.zh: 」然其服翫次於弘也。

translations.literal: " Yet his dress and play ranked below Hong.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet his finery ranked below Hong's.

sentences.zh: 君蒨辯於辭令，湘東王嘗出軍，有人將婦從者。

translations.literal: Junqian was sharp in repartee; Prince of Xiangdong once led the army out and someone brought his wife along.
translations.idiomatic: Junqian was quick with words; once when the prince marched out someone brought his wife.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「才愧李陵，未能先誅女子，將非孫武，遂欲驅戰婦人。

translations.literal: The prince said, "Talent shames Li Ling — unable to execute the women first; generalship shames Sun Wu — intending to drive the women to battle.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Talent shames Li Ling — I cannot kill the women first; generalship shames Sun Wu — I would drive women to war.

sentences.zh: 」君蒨應聲曰：「項籍壯士，猶有虞兮之愛，紀信成功，亦資姬人之力。

translations.literal: " Junqian answered at once, "Xiang Yu the stalwart still had love for Yu Ji; Ji Xin succeeded with help from the palace woman's strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Junqian answered, "Xiang Yu still loved Yu Ji; Ji Xin won with a palace woman's aid.

sentences.zh: 」君蒨文冠一府，特有輕豔之才，新聲巧變，人多諷習，竟卒於官。

translations.literal: " Junqian's letters led the office and he had special talent for light elegance; new songs clever in change — many sang and learned them — he finally died in office.
translations.idiomatic: " His writing led the office; his light songs spread widely — he died in office.

sentences.zh: 傅亮字季友，北地靈州人，晉司隸校尉咸之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Fu Liang, styled Jiyou, was a man of Ling Prefecture in Beidi — great-great-grandson of Jin Director of the Imperial Clan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang, styled Jiyou, came from Ling Prefecture in Beidi — fourth-generation descendant of Jin Director Xian.

sentences.zh: 父瑗以學業知名，位至安成太守。

translations.literal: Father Yuan was known for learning and reached Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan was a scholar and reached administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 瑗與郗超善，超常造瑗，見二子迪及亮。

translations.literal: Yuan was friendly with Chi Chao; Chao often visited Yuan and saw the two sons Di and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan befriended Chi Chao, who often visited and saw sons Di and Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮年四五歲，超令人解衣使持去，初無吝色。

translations.literal: Liang was four or five; Chao had someone undress him and carry him off — at first no sign of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was four or five when Chao had servants carry him off — he showed no reluctance.

sentences.zh: 超謂瑗曰：「卿小兒才名位宦當遠踰于兄，然保家終在大者。

translations.literal: Chao told Yuan, "Your small son's talent, name, and office will far surpass his elder brother's — yet preserving the family will finally rest on the elder.
translations.idiomatic: Chao told Yuan, "Your younger son will outrank his brother — yet the family will rest on the elder.

sentences.zh: 」迪字長猷，宋初終五兵尚書，贈太常。

translations.literal: " Di, styled Changyou, at the start of Song ended as Minister of Five Arms — posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: " Di, styled Changyou, ended as Minister of Five Arms under Song — posthumously Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 亮博涉經史，尤善文辭。

translations.literal: Liang broadly dipped into classics and histories, especially skilled at letters.
translations.idiomatic: Liang read widely in classics and histories and excelled at prose.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，累遷中書黃門侍郎，直西省。

translations.literal: In Yixi he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat at the Yellow Gate, serving in the Western Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yixi he rose to Secretariat Attendant at the Yellow Gate in the Western Office.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝以其久直之勤勞，欲以為東陽郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song because of his long faithful labor wished to make him Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wished to make him administrator of Dongyang for long faithful service.

sentences.zh: 先以語迪，大喜告亮，亮不答，即馳見武帝，陳不樂出。

translations.literal: He first told Di; Di rejoiced and told Liang — Liang did not answer, immediately rode to see the Emperor and stated he did not wish to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He told Di first; Di rejoiced and told Liang — Liang rode at once to refuse leaving court.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「謂卿須祿耳，能如此，甚協所望也。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said, "I thought you needed salary — able to do thus, very much in accord with what is hoped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled, "I thought you wanted salary — this suits my hope.

sentences.zh: 」以為太尉從事中郎，掌記室。

translations.literal: " He was made Attendant in the Grand Marshal's office, in charge of the recorder's office.
translations.idiomatic: " He became Grand Marshal attendant in charge of the recorder's office.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，除侍中，領世子中庶子，加中書令。

translations.literal: When the Song state was first established he was made Palace Attendant and Tutor of the Heir with additional Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Song was founded he became Palace Attendant, Tutor of the Heir, and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從還壽陽，武帝有受禪意，而難於發言，乃集朝臣宴飲，從容曰：「桓玄暴篡，鼎命已移，我首唱大義，興復皇室，今年時衰暮，欲歸老京師，」群臣唯盛稱功德，莫曉此意。

translations.literal: Returning from Shouyang the Emperor had intent to accept abdication but found it hard to speak; he gathered court gentlemen to feast and drink and said at ease, "Huan Xuan violently usurped and the mandate moved; I first raised the great cause and restored the royal house — now years decline and evening comes; I wish to retire old to the capital," — the ministers only praised merit and virtue and did not understand this intent.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Shouyang the Emperor wished to accept abdication but could not say it; at a feast he said, "Huan Xuan usurped; I restored the house — now I am old and wish to retire," — ministers praised him and missed his meaning.

sentences.zh: 亮悟旨，日晚宮門已閉，叩扉請見曰：「臣暫宜還都。

translations.literal: Liang understood the intent; evening came and palace gates were closed — he knocked and requested audience, saying, "Your servant for a time should return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang understood; gates closed at evening — he knocked and said, "I should return to the capital for a time.

sentences.zh: 」帝知意，無復他言，直云：「須幾人自送？

translations.literal: The Emperor knew the intent and had no other words — only said, "How many men must escort themselves?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor understood and asked only, "How many men must escort you?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「須數十人。

translations.literal: " Liang said, "Several tens of men are needed.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said, "Several tens.

sentences.zh: 」於是奉辭。

translations.literal: " He thereupon took leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He took leave.

sentences.zh: 及出，夜見長星竟天，拊髀曰：「我常不信天文，今始驗矣。

translations.literal: On leaving, at night he saw a long star filling the sky and slapped his thigh, saying, "I always did not believe astronomy — now it is verified.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving at night he saw a long star span the sky and slapped his thigh: "I never believed omens — now one proves true.

sentences.zh: 」亮至都，即征帝入輔。

translations.literal: " Liang reached the capital and at once summoned the Emperor to enter and assist.
translations.idiomatic: " Reaching the capital he summoned the Emperor to enter as regent.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，加太子詹事，封建城縣公，入直中書省，專典詔命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu he was added Tutor of the Heir, enfeoffed Duke of Jianchang, entered the Secretariat in direct service, exclusively drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 1 he became Tutor of the Heir, Duke of Jianchang, entered the Secretariat, and drafted edicts alone.

sentences.zh: 以亮任總國權，聽於省見客。

translations.literal: Because Liang's charge summed state power he was permitted to receive guests in the office.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang held state power he could receive guests in office.

sentences.zh: 神獸門外，每旦車常數百兩。

translations.literal: Outside the Divine Beast Gate each dawn carts numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Divine Beast Gate hundreds of carts gathered each dawn.

sentences.zh: 武帝登庸之始，文筆皆是參軍滕演，北征廣固，悉委長史王誕，自此之後至於受命，表策文誥，皆亮辭也。

translations.literal: At the start of the Emperor's ascent all writing was by staff officer Teng Yan; on the northern expedition to Guanggu all was entrusted to Chief of Staff Wang Dan — from then until receiving the mandate, memorials, plans, writings, and proclamations were all Liang's words.
translations.idiomatic: Early writing was Teng Yan's; the Guanggu campaign went to Wang Dan — from then until abdication all edicts were Liang's.

sentences.zh: 演字彥將，南陽西鄂人，位至秘書監。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Yanjiang, was a man of Xi'e in Nanyang — reached Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Yanjiang, of Xi'e in Nanyang, became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，加亮尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year Liang was added Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Liang became Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 及帝不豫，與徐羨之、謝晦並受顧命，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was unwell he with Xu Xianzhi and Xie Hui together received the dying charge — granted twenty guard halberds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill he with Xianzhi and Hui received the dying charge — twenty guard halberds.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，進中書監、尚書令，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Lesser Emperor ascended he was promoted Director of the Secretariat and Minister, and Commandant Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lesser Emperor ascended he became Director, Minister, and Commandant Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 及文帝即位，加左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended he was added Grand Master of Splendor with office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended he received Grand Master of Splendor with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 司空府文武即為左光祿府，進爵始興郡公，固讓進封。

translations.literal: Minister of Works civil and military staff became the Grand Splendor office; advanced to Duke of Shixing and firmly declined further enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The Works staff became his Grand Splendor office; he became Duke of Shixing and declined further honors.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，帝將誅亮，先呼入見，省內密有報之者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia the Emperor was about to execute Liang and first summoned him to audience — within the office someone secretly reported.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 3 the Emperor meant to kill Liang and summoned him — someone inside warned him.

sentences.zh: 亮辭以嫂病暫還，遣信報徐羨之，因乘車出郭門，騎馬奔兄迪墓。

translations.literal: Liang declined on grounds of sister-in-law's illness and temporary return, sent word to Xu Xianzhi, then rode out the city gate, mounted horse and raced to elder brother Di's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Liang pleaded his sister-in-law's illness, warned Xianzhi, rode out the gate, and raced to Di's tomb.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉郭泓收之。

translations.literal: Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Guo Hong arrested him.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Guo Hong of Garrison Cavalry arrested him.

sentences.zh: 初至廣莫門，上亦使以詔謂曰：「以公江陵之誠，當使諸子無恙。

translations.literal: At first reaching the Broad Mo Gate the Emperor also sent edict saying, "For your loyalty at Jiangling your sons should be unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Broad Mo Gate an edict came: "For your loyalty at Jiangling your sons will be spared.

sentences.zh: 」亮讀詔訖曰：「亮受先帝布衣之眷，遂蒙顧托。

translations.literal: Liang finished reading the edict and said, "Liang received the former Emperor's favor from common cloth and then received entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: Liang read the edict and said, "I received the late Emperor's favor from common cloth and his dying trust.

sentences.zh: 黜昏立明，社稷之計。

translations.literal: Deposing the dim and establishing the bright — the plan for altars and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing the unworthy and raising the worthy — that was the plan for the realm.

sentences.zh: 欲加之罪，其無辭乎。

translations.literal: Wishing to add crime — is there no wording?
translations.idiomatic: If you wish guilt, words are easy.

sentences.zh: 」於是伏誅，妻子流建安。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was executed; wife and children were exiled to Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: " He was executed; wife and children exiled to Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 亮之方貴，兄迪每深誡焉，而不能從。

translations.literal: When Liang was rising in honor elder brother Di always deeply admonished but he could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang rose, Di admonished him but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及見世路屯險，著論名曰演慎。

translations.literal: Seeing the world's path perilous he wrote a treatise called Practicing Caution.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing peril on the path of power he wrote Practicing Caution.

sentences.zh: 及少帝失德，內懷憂懼。

translations.literal: When the Lesser Emperor lost virtue he harbored worry and fear within.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lesser Emperor lost virtue he was inwardly afraid.

sentences.zh: 直宿禁中，睹夜蛾赴燭，作感物賦以寄意。

translations.literal: On night duty in the forbidden palace he saw moths fly to the candle and composed the Rhapsody on Moved Things to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: On night duty he saw moths fly to the candle and wrote Rhapsody on Moved Things.

sentences.zh: 初奉大駕，道路賦詩三首，其一篇有悔懼之辭。

translations.literal: At first escorting the great carriage he composed three road poems — one piece had words of regret and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the imperial carriage he wrote three road poems — one full of regret and fear.

sentences.zh: 自知傾覆，求退無由，又作辛有、穆生、董仲道贊，稱其見微之美云。

translations.literal: Knowing himself overturned and seeking retreat without path, he again composed encomia to Xin You, Mu Sheng, and Dong Zhongdao, praising their beauty of seeing the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing ruin was near and unable to retreat, he praised Xin You, Mu Sheng, and Dong Zhongdao for foresight.

sentences.zh: 隆字伯祚，亮族兄也。

translations.literal: Long, styled Bozuo, was Liang's clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Long, styled Bozuo, was Liang's clansman.

sentences.zh: 曾祖晞，司徒屬。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Xi was staff officer to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Xi served the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 父祖並早卒。

translations.literal: Father and grandfather both died early.
translations.idiomatic: Father and grandfather both died young.

sentences.zh: 隆少孤貧，有學行。

translations.literal: Long was orphaned young and poor, with learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, Long had learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，年四十，為孟昶建威參軍，累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the start of Yixi, age forty, he was staff officer to Meng Chang's Establishing Might command, repeatedly promoted to Left Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At Yixi's start, aged forty, he served Meng Chang and rose to Left Director.

sentences.zh: 以族弟亮為僕射，緦服不得相臨，徙太子率更令。

translations.literal: Because clansman Liang was Vice Director, in mourning garb of the fourth month he could not face one another — moved to Commandant of the Heir's Rate Revision.
translations.idiomatic: Because cousin Liang was Vice Director, fourth-month mourning barred them from meeting — Long became Heir's Rate Revision Commandant.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，為御史中丞，甚得司直之體，轉司徒左長史。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanjia he was Censor-in-Chief, very obtaining the upright censor's substance, then moved to Left Chief of Staff of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanjia's start he was Censor-in-Chief with true uprightness, then Left Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 會稽剡縣人黃初妻趙打殺息載妻王遇赦，王有父母及男稱女葉，依法徙趙二千里外。

translations.literal: Huang Chu of Yan in Kuaiji killed his daughter-in-law Wang on amnesty; Wang had parents and a son named Ye and daughter Ye — by law Zhao was exiled two thousand li beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chu's wife Zhao in Yan of Kuaiji killed daughter-in-law Wang on amnesty; by law Zhao was exiled two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 隆議曰：「禮律之興，本之自然。

translations.literal: Long debated, "Rites and law arise from what is natural.
translations.idiomatic: Long argued, "Rite and law arise from nature.

sentences.zh: 求之情理，非從天墮，非從地出。

translations.literal: Seeking it in feeling and principle — it does not fall from heaven, does not spring from earth.
translations.idiomatic: Seek them in feeling and principle — they neither fall from heaven nor rise from earth.

sentences.zh: 父子至親，分形同氣，稱之於載，即載之于趙。

translations.literal: Father and son are utmost kin — sharing form and sharing breath; Ye's claim on Zai is Zai's claim on Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son share flesh and breath; Ye's tie to Zai is Zai's tie to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 雖言三世，為體猶一。

translations.literal: Though called three generations, the substance is still one.
translations.idiomatic: Though called three generations, they are one body.

sentences.zh: 稱雖創钜痛深，固無讎祖之義。

translations.literal: Though Ye suffered fresh wound and deep pain, solidly there is no meaning of avenging ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ye grieved deeply, he owed ancestors no blood vengeance.

sentences.zh: 向使石厚之子，日磾之孫，砥鋒挺鍔，不與二祖同戴天日，則石碏、秺侯何得流名百代。

translations.literal: Suppose Shi Hou's son or Ri Di's grandson whetted blade and bared sword and did not share heaven and sun with the two ancestors — then Shi Que and the Marquis of Di would not flow their names through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: If Shi Hou's son or Ri Di's grandson drew blade against forebears, Shi Que and the Di marquis would not be famed for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 舊令言殺人父母，徙之二千里外，不施父子孫祖明矣。

translations.literal: The old order says killing a man's parents — exile two thousand li beyond — the non-application to father, son, grandson, and ancestor is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Old law exiles parent-killers two thousand li — it clearly excludes father, son, grandson, and ancestor.

sentences.zh: 趙當避王期功千里外耳。

translations.literal: Zhao should avoid Wang's mourning period only a thousand li beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao need only avoid Wang's mourning circle by a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 令亦云凡流徙者，同籍親近欲相隨者聽之。

translations.literal: The order also says all who are exiled — close kin on the same register wishing to follow may do so.
translations.idiomatic: The code also lets close kin on the same register follow exiles.

sentences.zh: 此又大通情體，因親以教愛也。

translations.literal: This again greatly extends feeling and substance — teaching love through kin.
translations.idiomatic: That too follows feeling — teaching love through kin.

sentences.zh: 趙既流移，載為人子，何得不從？

translations.literal: Zhao already in exile — as a son how can Zai not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao is already exiled — as a son how can Zai not follow?

sentences.zh: 載從而稱不行，豈名教所許？

translations.literal: Zai follows yet Ye does not go — how is name-teaching permitted?
translations.idiomatic: If Zai follows and Ye stays, how does teaching permit it?

sentences.zh: 如此，稱、趙竟不可分。

translations.literal: Thus Ye and Zhao ultimately cannot be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and Zhao cannot be split.

sentences.zh: 趙雖內愧終身，稱沈痛沒齒，孫祖之義，自不得以永絕，事理然也。

translations.literal: Though Zhao inwardly ashamed all life, Ye sinks in pain to the gums — the meaning of grandson and ancestor by itself cannot be forever cut — principle and affair are so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao may shame inwardly all her life and Ye grieve to the grave — yet grandson and ancestor cannot be severed forever; such is principle.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 出為義興太守，有能名。

translations.literal: Sent out as Administrator of Yixing — noted ability.
translations.idiomatic: As administrator of Yixing he earned a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 拜左戶尚書，坐正直受節假，對人未至委出，白衣領職。

translations.literal: Made Left Minister of Households — for on regular duty receiving leave of absence, before the person arrived he delegated out — served in office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Made Left Minister of Households — he took leave before the substitute arrived and served in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太常，文帝以新撰禮論付隆，使更下意。

translations.literal: Soon moved to Minister of Ceremonies; Emperor Wen gave the newly compiled Rites Discussion to Long to further revise.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Minister of Ceremonies; Emperor Wen gave him the new Rites Discussion to revise.

sentences.zh: 隆表上五十二事。

translations.literal: Long memorialized fifty-two items.
translations.idiomatic: Long submitted fifty-two items.

sentences.zh: 後致仕，拜光祿大夫，歸老於家。

translations.literal: Later he retired, made Grand Master of Splendor, and returned old to home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Grand Master of Splendor and went home.

sentences.zh: 手不釋卷，博學多通，特精三禮。

translations.literal: Hand never leaving scroll — broad learning and much mastery, especially refined in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He never put books down — learned and masterful, especially in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 年八十三卒。

translations.literal: Age eighty-three he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟

translations.literal: Tan Daoji
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji

sentences.zh: 檀道濟，高平金鄉人也，世居京口。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji was a man of Jinxiang in Gaoping — family long lived at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji came from Jinxiang in Gaoping; his family had long lived at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，居喪備禮，奉兄姊以和謹稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, in mourning he kept full rites and served elder brother and sisters with harmony and care — so he was named.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he kept mourning rites fully and served siblings with harmony — hence his reputation.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝建義，道濟與兄韶祗等從平京城，俱參武帝建武將軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised the righteous cause Daoji with elder brother Shao and others followed in pacifying the capital — all joined the Emperor's Establishing Might staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu raised the cause Daoji and elder brother Shao helped pacify the capital on his Establishing Might staff.

sentences.zh: 累遷太尉參軍，封作唐縣男。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Grand Marshal staff officer — enfeoffed Baron of Zuotang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Marshal staff officer and was enfeoffed Baron of Zuotang.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年，武帝北伐，道濟為前鋒，所至望風降服。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi the Emperor marched north; Daoji was vanguard — wherever he reached they surrendered at sight of his flags.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 12 on the northern march Daoji led the vanguard — places surrendered at his approach.

sentences.zh: 徑進洛陽，議者謂所獲俘囚，應悉戮以為京觀。

translations.literal: Pressing straight to Luoyang, debaters said captives taken should all be slaughtered to make a capital mound.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Luoyang, some said all captives should be slaughtered for a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 道濟曰：「伐罪吊人，正在今日。

translations.literal: Daoji said, "Punishing crime and comforting the people — right in this day.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji said, "Punish the guilty and comfort the people — that is today's task.

sentences.zh: 」皆釋而遣之。

translations.literal: " All were released and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: " All were released.

sentences.zh: 於是中原感悅，歸者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon the central plains were moved and pleased — those who returned were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The central plains rejoiced — many returned to Song.

sentences.zh: 長安平，以為琅邪內史。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified he was made Internal Administrator of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an fell he became internal administrator of Langya.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，以佐命功，改封永修縣公，位丹陽尹、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the mandate, for founding merit he was changed to Duke of Yongxiu — post Governor of Danyang and Commandant Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: At abdication, for founding merit he became Duke of Yongxiu, governor of Danyang, and Commandant Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 武帝不豫，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was unwell he was granted twenty guard halberds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill he received twenty guard halberds.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之等謀廢立，諷道濟入朝，告以將廢廬陵王義真，道濟屢陳不可，竟不納。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and others plotted deposition — they hinted Daoji enter court and told him they would depose Prince of Luling Yizhen; Daoji repeatedly stated it could not be — in the end not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and others plotting deposition summoned Daoji and told him of deposing Prince Yizhen; Daoji refused repeatedly — they ignored him.

sentences.zh: 將廢帝夜，道濟入領軍府就謝晦宿，晦悚息不得眠。

translations.literal: The night they would depose the Emperor Daoji entered the Commandant's office and lodged with Xie Hui; Hui was fearful and breathless, unable to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: The night of the deposition Daoji slept at Xie Hui's command office; Hui lay awake in fear.

sentences.zh: 道濟寢便睡熟，晦以此服之。

translations.literal: Daoji slept at once deeply — Hui thereby submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji slept soundly — Hui admired his calm.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，給鼓吹一部，進封武陵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended he was granted one set of drums and pipes — advanced to Duke of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended he received drums and pipes and became Duke of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 固辭進封。

translations.literal: Firmly declined further enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He declined further honors.

sentences.zh: 道濟素與王弘善，時被遇方深，道濟彌相結附，每構羨之等，弘亦雅仗之。

translations.literal: Daoji was always friendly with Wang Hong; at that time favored deeply, Daoji all the more attached himself — whenever he framed Xianzhi and the others Hong also relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji was close to Wang Hong; deeply favored, he attached himself and with Hong framed Xianzhi's faction.

sentences.zh: 上將誅徐羨之等，召道濟欲使西討。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to execute Xu Xianzhi and the others and summoned Daoji wishing to make him march west to attack.
translations.idiomatic: About to kill Xianzhi and others, the Emperor summoned Daoji for a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 王華曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Wang Hua said, "Cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua said, "No.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「道濟從人者也，曩非創謀，撫而使之，必將無慮。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "Daoji follows men's lead — he was not among the first plotters; comfort and send him and he will surely be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Daoji follows others — he did not plot first; reassure him and he will serve.

sentences.zh: 」道濟至之明日，上誅羨之、亮。

translations.literal: The day after Daoji arrived the Emperor executed Xianzhi and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Daoji arrived the Emperor killed Xianzhi and Liang.

sentences.zh: 既而使道濟與中領軍到彥之前驅西伐，上問策於道濟。

translations.literal: Presently he sent Daoji with Central Army Commander Dao Yan as vanguard west to attack; the Emperor asked Daoji for strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Daoji with Dao Yan west; the Emperor asked his strategy.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣昔與謝晦同從北征，入關十策，晦有其九。

translations.literal: He answered, "Your servant formerly with Xie Hui together followed the northern expedition — entering the pass, of ten stratagems Hui had nine.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I campaigned north with Xie Hui — of ten plans entering the pass, Hui had nine.

sentences.zh: 才略明練，殆難與敵；

translations.literal: Talent and plan bright and practiced — probably hard to match;
translations.idiomatic: His talent and plans are sharp — hard to match;

sentences.zh: 然未嘗孤軍決勝，戎事恐非其長。

translations.literal: yet he has never alone decided victory in army affairs — military affairs perhaps not his length.
translations.idiomatic: yet he never wins alone in the field — battle may not be his strength.

sentences.zh: 臣悉晦智，晦悉臣勇。

translations.literal: Your servant knows Hui's wisdom; Hui knows your servant's courage.
translations.idiomatic: I know Hui's wit; Hui knows my courage.

sentences.zh: 今奉王命外討，必未陣而禽。

translations.literal: Now receiving the king's command to attack outward — before battle he will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Now under royal command I attack — before battle he will be taken.

sentences.zh: 」時晦本謂道濟與羨之同誅，忽聞來上，遂不戰自潰。

translations.literal: At that time Hui originally thought Daoji would be executed with Xianzhi — suddenly hearing he came up — thereupon without battle self-collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui expected Daoji dead with Xianzhi — hearing he came, his army collapsed without fighting.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was moved to General Who Conquers the South, office equal to the Three Excellencies with full staff, and Governor of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he became General Who Conquers the South with rank equal to the Three Excellencies and governor of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉八年，到彥之侵魏，已平河南，復失之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia Dao Yan invaded Wei — already pacified Henan, again lost it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 8 Dao Yan invaded Wei — took Henan, then lost it.

sentences.zh: 道濟都督征討諸軍事，北略地，轉戰至濟上，魏軍盛，遂克滑台。

translations.literal: Daoji overall commanded the punitive expedition, advancing north and fighting to the Ji River — Wei armies were strong and he took Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji commanded the punitive expedition, fought to the Ji River, and took Huatai despite strong Wei forces.

sentences.zh: 道濟時與魏軍三十餘戰多捷，軍至曆城，以資運竭乃還。

translations.literal: Daoji at the time with Wei armies fought more than thirty battles with many victories — army reached Licheng; because supplies and transport were exhausted he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Wei more than thirty times with many wins, reached Licheng, then retreated when supplies ran out.

sentences.zh: 時人降魏者具說糧食已罄，於是士卒憂懼，莫有固志。

translations.literal: Men of the time who defected to Wei all said grain was already exhausted — thereupon soldiers worried and feared, none had firm will.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors told Wei grain was gone — soldiers panicked and lost heart.

sentences.zh: 道濟夜唱籌量沙，以所余少米散其上。

translations.literal: Daoji by night ordered measuring sand, scattering the remaining little rice on top.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji by night had sand measured and the last rice scattered on top.

sentences.zh: 及旦，魏軍謂資糧有餘，故不復追，以降者妄，斬以徇。

translations.literal: At dawn Wei armies thought supplies and grain had surplus — therefore did not pursue further; because defectors lied they were beheaded to warn.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Wei thought supplies abundant and did not pursue; liars were beheaded as warning.

sentences.zh: 時道濟兵寡弱，軍中大懼。

translations.literal: At that time Daoji's army was few and weak — great fear in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji's army was weak and terrified.

sentences.zh: 道濟乃命軍士悉甲，身白服乘輿，徐出周邊。

translations.literal: Daoji then ordered soldiers all armored; he himself in white clothes rode the carriage and slowly went the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji ordered full armor; he rode in white clothes and slowly circled the camp.

sentences.zh: 魏軍懼有伏，不敢逼，乃歸。

translations.literal: Wei armies feared ambush and did not dare press — thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei feared ambush and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道濟雖不克定河南，全軍而反，雄名大振。

translations.literal: Daoji though he did not settle Henan, returned with the whole army — great fame shook.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not hold Henan, he brought the whole army home — fame shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 魏甚憚之，圖之以禳鬼。

translations.literal: Wei greatly feared him and plotted to use ghost-appeasement against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei greatly feared him and plotted sorcery against him.

sentences.zh: 還進位司空，鎮尋陽。

translations.literal: On return advanced to Minister of Works, garrisoned Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he became Minister of Works and garrisoned Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 道濟立功前朝，威名甚重，左右腹心並經百戰，諸子又有才氣，朝廷疑畏之。

translations.literal: Daoji achieved merit in the former dynasty — prestige and name very heavy; close confidants all had passed a hundred battles — sons also had talent and spirit — court suspected and feared.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji's old merit, fame, veteran staff, and talented sons made court fear him.

sentences.zh: 時人或目之曰：「安知非司馬仲達也。」

translations.literal: Men of the time pointed at him saying, "How know he is not Sima Zhongda?"
translations.idiomatic: Men said, "Who says he is not another Sima Yi?"

sentences.zh: 文帝寢疾累年，屢經危殆，領軍劉湛貪執朝政，慮道濟為異說，又彭城王義康亦慮宮車晏駕，道濟不復可制。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen bedridden for years repeatedly near death — Commandant of the Guard Liu Zhan greedy to hold court government, fearing Daoji as different opinion; also Prince of Pengcheng Yikang feared when the imperial carriage peacefully halted Daoji could no longer be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen lay ill for years; Liu Zhan grasped court power and feared Daoji; Prince Yikang of Pengcheng feared Daoji if the Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 十二年，上疾篤，會魏軍南伐，召道濟入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Emperor gravely ill — meeting Wei armies south invading he summoned Daoji to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, gravely ill as Wei invaded south, he summoned Daoji.

sentences.zh: 其妻向氏曰：「夫高世之勳，道家所忌，今無事相召，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Xiang said, "Merit surpassing the age — the Daoist path forbids it; now summoned without affair — disaster probably arrives.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Xiang said, "Merit too great is forbidden — summoned without cause, disaster comes.

sentences.zh: 」及至，上已間。

translations.literal: When he arrived the Emperor was already recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the Emperor had recovered.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，將遣還鎮，下渚未發，有似鷦鳥集船悲鳴。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirteenth year about to be sent back to garrison — below the ford not yet departed — something like wrens gathered on the boat crying mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of year 13, about to return, wrens gathered on the boat crying mournfully before he sailed.

sentences.zh: 會上疾動，義康矯詔召入祖道，收付廷尉，及其子給事黃門侍郎植、司徒從事中郎粲、太子舍人混、征北主簿承伯、秘書郎中尊等八人並誅。

translations.literal: Meeting the Emperor's illness stirring, Yikang forged edict summoning him to the farewell feast, arrested and delivered to the Court of Justice — with his sons Attendant of the Yellow Gate Zhi, Staff Officer of the Minister of Education Can, Heir's Household Attendant Hun, Chief Clerk of the Northern Expedition Chengbai, Secretariat Attendant Zun — eight men all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor relapsed, Yikang forged an edict, arrested Daoji at his farewell feast, and executed him with sons Zhi, Can, Hun, Chengbai, and Zun — eight in all.

sentences.zh: 時人歌曰：「可憐白浮鳩，枉殺檀江州。

translations.literal: Men of the time sang, "Pitiable white floating dove — wrongly killed Tan of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Men sang, "Pitiable white dove — wrongly killed Tan of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」道濟死日，建鄴地震白毛生。

translations.literal: The day Daoji died Jianye earthquake — white hair grew.
translations.idiomatic: The day Daoji died Jianye shook and white hair sprouted.

sentences.zh: 又誅司空參軍薛肜、高進之，並道濟心腹也。

translations.literal: Again executed Minister of Works staff officers Xue Tong and Gao Jin — both Daoji's trusted confidants.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers Xue Tong and Gao Jin, Daoji's confidants, were also killed.

sentences.zh: 道濟見收，憤怒氣盛，目光如炬，俄爾間引飲一斛。

translations.literal: Daoji on arrest — angry breath swelled — eyes like torches — in a moment between he drank a hu.
translations.idiomatic: Arrested, Daoji raged — eyes like torches — and drank a hu in a breath.

sentences.zh: 乃脫幘投地，曰：「乃壞汝萬里長城。

translations.literal: Then he removed cap and threw it to the ground, saying, "You have ruined your ten-thousand-li long wall.
translations.idiomatic: He tore off his cap and cried, "You have ruined your ten-thousand-li long wall.

sentences.zh: 」魏人聞之，皆曰：「道濟已死，吳子輩不足復憚」。
