translations.literal: Wei men hearing all said, "Daoji already dead — Wu sons not worth further fear."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Daoji is dead — Song's sons need no further fear."

sentences.zh: 自是頻歲南伐，有飲馬長江之志。

translations.literal: From then year after year south invading — had ambition to water horses at the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: From then Wei invaded south yearly, aiming to water horses at the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 文帝問殷景仁曰：「誰可繼道濟？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen asked Yin Jingren, "Who can succeed Daoji?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen asked Yin Jingren, "Who succeeds Daoji?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「道濟以累有戰功，故致威名，余但未任耳。

translations.literal: He answered, "Daoji because repeated battle merit therefore obtained prestige and name — the rest are not yet tested.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Daoji's fame came from repeated victories — the rest are untested.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「不然，昔李廣在朝，匈奴不敢南望，後繼者復有幾人？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Not so — formerly Li Guang in court, the Xiongnu dared not look south — how many followed after?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "No — when Li Guang was at court the Xiongnu dared not look south — how many followed him?

sentences.zh: 」二十七年，魏軍至瓜步，文帝登石頭城望，甚有憂色。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Wei armies reached Guabu — Emperor Wen ascended Shitou city and looked — very worried in expression.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 Wei reached Guabu — Emperor Wen looked from Shitou, deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「若道濟在，豈至此！」

translations.literal: Sighed, "If Daoji were here — how reach this!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "If Daoji were here, it would not come to this!"

sentences.zh: 兄 濟

translations.literal: Elder brother Ji
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Ji

sentences.zh: 韶字令孫，以平桓玄功封巴丘縣侯。

translations.literal: Shao, styled Lingsun, for pacifying Huan Xuan enfeoffed Marquis of Baqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, styled Lingsun, was enfeoffed Marquis of Baqiu for suppressing Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 從征廣固，率所領先登，位琅邪內史。

translations.literal: Following the Guanggu expedition he led his command first to ascend — post Internal Administrator of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: On the Guanggu campaign he led his men first up the walls — then internal administrator of Langya.

sentences.zh: 從討盧循，以功更封宜陽縣侯，拜江州刺史，以罪免。

translations.literal: Following the suppression of Lu Xun — for merit changed to Marquis of Yiyang — made Governor of Jiang — removed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing Lu Xun he became Marquis of Yiyang and governor of Jiang — then dismissed for crime.

sentences.zh: 韶嗜酒貪橫，所蒞無政績，上嘉其合門從義，道濟又有大功，故特見寵授。

translations.literal: Shao loved wine and was greedy and overbearing — wherever he held office no achievement — the Emperor praised the clan's joining the righteous cause and Daoji also had great merit — therefore specially seen in favor and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shao drank, grasped, and ruled badly — yet the clan's loyalty and Daoji's merit won him favor.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: Died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子臻字系宗，位員外郎，臻子珪。

translations.literal: Son Zhen, styled Xizong, post Outside Office Gentleman — Zhen's son Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhen, styled Xizong, was an outside-office gentleman — Zhen's son Gui.

sentences.zh: 濟孫 珪

translations.literal: Ji's grandson Gui
translations.idiomatic: Ji's grandson Gui

sentences.zh: 珪字伯玉，位沅南令。

translations.literal: Gui, styled Boyu, post Magistrate of Yuannan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Boyu, was magistrate of Yuannan.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，王僧虔為吏部尚書，以珪為征北板行參軍。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui Wang Sengqian was Director of Personnel — made Gui staff officer on the Northern Expedition board.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui Wang Sengqian as Director of Personnel made Gui a northern staff officer.

sentences.zh: 珪訴僧虔求祿不得，與僧虔書曰：「僕一門雖謝文通，乃忝武達。

translations.literal: Gui complained to Sengqian seeking salary without success and wrote Sengqian, "Your servant's gate though lacks Wentong yet disgraces Wuda.
translations.idiomatic: Gui begged salary in vain and wrote Sengqian, "My house lacks literary fame but claims martial honor.

sentences.zh: 群從姑叔，三媾帝姻，而令子侄餓死，遂不荷潤。

translations.literal: Clansmen and uncles — three marriages with the imperial house — yet let sons and nephews starve — finally no moistening.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen thrice married imperial princesses — yet my nephews starve without aid.

sentences.zh: 蟬腹龜腸，為日已久。

translations.literal: Cicada belly turtle intestine — already long the day.
translations.idiomatic: My belly is empty as a cicada's — long the day.

sentences.zh: 饑彪能嚇，人遽與肉，餓驎不噬，誰為落毛。

translations.literal: Hungry leopard can frighten — men hasten to give meat; starving qilin does not bite — who will drop feathers?
translations.idiomatic: A hungry leopard still frightens men into feeding it; a starving qilin will not bite — who will drop a feather?

sentences.zh: 雖復孤微，百世國士，姻媾位宦，亦不後物。

translations.literal: Though again solitary and slight — for a hundred generations a knight of the state; marriage and office also not behind others.
translations.idiomatic: Though lowly, we are knights of the realm for a hundred generations — marriage and office match others.

sentences.zh: 尚書同堂姊為江夏王妃，檀珪同堂姑為南譙王妃；

translations.literal: Director's paternal cousin was consort to Prince of Jiangxia — Tan Gui's paternal aunt was consort to Prince of Nanqiao;
translations.idiomatic: Your paternal cousin was Princess of Jiangxia; my paternal aunt was Princess of Nanqiao;

sentences.zh: 尚書伯為江州，檀珪祖亦為江州。

translations.literal: Director's elder uncle was Governor of Jiang — Tan Gui's grandfather also Governor of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Your uncle governed Jiang; my grandfather governed Jiang.

sentences.zh: 僕于尚書人地本懸，至於婚宦皆不殊絕。

translations.literal: Your servant with the Director in men and land originally suspended — reaching marriage and office all not extremely different.
translations.idiomatic: You and I differ in rank and land — yet marriage and office hardly differ.

sentences.zh: 今通塞雖異，猶忝氣類，尚書何事為爾見苦。

translations.literal: Today though blocked and open differ — still disgrace the same breath and kind — Director why act thus bitter toward me?
translations.idiomatic: Fortune differs now — yet we share one breath — why torment me?

sentences.zh: 」僧虔報書曰：「吾與足下素無怨憾，何以相苦？

translations.literal: Sengqian replied, "I with you plain have no resentment — why mutually bitter?
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian replied, "I bear you no grudge — why this bitterness?

sentences.zh: 直是意有左右耳。

translations.literal: Simply intention has left and right ear.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply bias of intent.

sentences.zh: 」乃用為安成郡丞。

translations.literal: " He then employed him as Assistant Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made him assistant administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 兄 祗

translations.literal: Elder brother Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Zhi

sentences.zh: 祗字恭叔，與兄韶弟道濟俱參義舉，封西昌縣侯，歷位廣陵相。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Gongshu, with elder brother Shao and younger brother Daoji all joined the righteous rising — enfeoffed Marquis of Xichang — served as Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Gongshu, with brothers Shao and Daoji joined the righteous rising, was enfeoffed Marquis of Xichang, and governed Guangling.

sentences.zh: 義熙十年，亡命司馬國璠兄弟自北徐州界潛得過淮，因天陰闇，夜率百許人緣廣陵城入，叫喚直上聽事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yixi outlaws Sima Guofan and brothers from Northern Xuzhou border secretly crossed the Huai — because sky was dark and dim, at night led about a hundred men along Guangling wall to enter, shouting straight up to the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 10 outlaws Sima Guofan and brothers slipped across the Huai; under cover of dark night about a hundred men scaled Guangling's wall shouting for the hall.

sentences.zh: 祗被射傷股，語左右曰：「賊乘暗得入，欲掩我不備，但打五鼓懼之，曉必走矣。

translations.literal: Zhi was shot wounded in the thigh — told attendants, "Bandits by dark gained entry — wish to surprise my unpreparedness — only beat five drums to frighten them — at dawn they will surely flee.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was shot in the thigh and told attendants, "They entered in the dark to surprise us — beat five drums; at dawn they will flee.

sentences.zh: 」賊聞鼓鳴，直謂為曉，乃奔散，追殺百餘人。

translations.literal: Bandits hearing drums directly thought it dawn — thereupon scattered in flight — pursued and killed more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing drums they thought dawn had come and fled — over a hundred were killed in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，為領軍。

translations.literal: When the Song state was first established he was Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Song was founded he became Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 祗性矜豪，樂在外放恣，不願內職，不得志，發疾不自療，其年卒於廣陵。

translations.literal: Zhi by nature was proud and lavish — loved being outside unrestrained, unwilling for inner office — unfulfilled, fell ill without treating himself — that year died at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and lavish, Zhi loved freedom outside court, hated inner office, sickened in frustration without treatment, and died at Guangling that year.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威侯。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Marquis Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Marquis Wei.

sentences.zh: 傳嗣至齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: Transmission of succession to Qi receiving abdication — state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief passed down until Qi took the throne and abolished it.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自晉網不綱，主威莫樹，亂基王室，毒被江左。

translations.literal: The commentary says: From Jin's net not governing, lordly authority not established — disorder rooted in the royal house, poison spread across the east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: When Jin's authority failed and royal power collapsed, disorder rooted in the house and poison spread across the south.

sentences.zh: 宋武一朝創業，事屬橫流，改易紊章，歸於平道。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song in one morning created enterprise — affairs belonged to the crosscurrent — changing confused chapters, returning to the level path.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song in one stroke founded the dynasty amid chaos, straightened tangled laws, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 以建武、永平之風，變太元、隆安之俗，此蓋文宣公之為乎。

translations.literal: With Jianwu and Yongping's wind changing Taiyuan and Long'an's custom — this probably was Duke Wenxuan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: With the spirit of Jianwu and Yongping he changed the habits of Taiyuan and Long'an — that was likely Duke Wenxuan's work.

sentences.zh: 其配饗清廟，豈徒然也？

translations.literal: His paired sacrifice in the Clear Temple — how merely for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: His place in the Clear Temple was no empty honor.

sentences.zh: 若夫怙才驕物，公旦其猶病諸，而以劉祥居之，斯亡亦為幸焉。

translations.literal: As for relying on talent and insulting others — even the Duke of Zhou perhaps still had this illness, yet to place Liu Xiang in it — such death was also fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou might fault pride in talent — yet for Liu Xiang such a death was mercy.

sentences.zh: 秀之行己有道，可謂位無虛授。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi in conduct had the Way — one may say the post was not vainly granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi walked the Way — his office was not wasted.

sentences.zh: 當徐、傅二公跪承顧托，若使死而可再，固當赴蹈為期。

translations.literal: When the two lords Xu and Fu knelt receiving entrustment — if death could come again they would surely have gone and trodden as appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu and Fu knelt to receive the dying charge, had death reversed they would have returned to fulfill it.

sentences.zh: 及至處權定機，當震主之地，甫欲攘抑後禍，禦蔽身災，使桐宮有卒迫之痛，淮王非中霧之疾，若以社稷為存亡，則義異於此。

translations.literal: Reaching the place where power was held and the moment fixed — ground that shook the lord — just wishing to push down later disaster and ward off personal calamity, making the Tong Palace have the pain of sudden end, Prince of Huai not the illness of mid-mist — if taking altars and grain as survival and extinction, righteousness differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once they held power at the lord's side, they tried only to ward off later ruin and personal disaster — not to spare the deposed emperor sudden agony or the Prince of Huai a mysterious death; if the realm's survival was the measure, their conduct falls short.

sentences.zh: 湛之、孝嗣臨機不決，既以敗國，且以殞身，「反受其亂」，斯其效也。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi and Xiaosi at the critical moment did not decide — already thereby ruining the state and also perishing the body — "in turn receiving their disorder" — such is the effect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi and Xiaosi failed at the decisive moment — ruining the state and losing their lives; "they reaped the chaos they helped sow."

sentences.zh: 道濟始因錄用，故得忘瑕，晚困大名，以至顛覆。

translations.literal: Daoji at first because recorded use therefore could forget flaws — late trapped by great name, reaching overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji at first was used despite flaws, but in the end his great name destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 韶、祗克傳胤嗣，其木雁之間乎。」

translations.literal: Shao and Zhi able to transmit heirs — between wooden goose perhaps?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Zhi passed down their lines — perhaps mere wooden geese in the rite?"
